title: Walkthrough: from install to results
text: This page runs through one complete cycle: install, run the baseline package once as a test of the installation, define a scenario, run it, and read the results in the dashboard, which shows the scenario against the baseline. A scenario can be defined three ways (section 4); the walkthrough follows the spreadsheet route first and the command-line route after it. Commands are for macOS, Linux and the container; on Windows replace scripts/run_model_unix.sh with scripts\run_model_windows.bat and julia with .bsat_local\julia\bin\julia.exe. All paths are relative to the repository root.

title: Walkthrough: from install to results
text:
1. Install
Pick one of the three tracks: Cloud and Docker, Local: macOS and Linux or Local: Windows. Each ends with a working Julia environment for code/model/ and the bsat R environment and, optionally, the bsat-dashboard Python environment.
The commands below are typed at a terminal prompt and run by pressing Enter. In a codespace the terminal is the panel at the bottom of the VS Code window in the browser, usually already open when the codespace starts; if it is not there, open it from the menu with Terminal > New Terminal (the menu sits behind the three-line icon at the top left) or with the keyboard shortcut Ctrl+` (the backtick key). On a local Windows install the terminal is a Command Prompt, on macOS the Terminal application (Applications > Utilities, or search “Terminal” in Spotlight), on Linux your usual terminal application. Every command assumes the repository root is the current directory: a codespace starts there, and on a local install you cd into the repository folder first.
In a codespace, install nothing. VS Code offers to install extensions, and the R extension in particular asks to install an R language server and then reports that it failed. Decline or close every such prompt and dismiss the error; the container already carries Julia, R and the dashboard environment, and nothing in the model depends on those extensions. Cloud and Docker has the detail.

title: Walkthrough: from install to results
text:
2. License
The PATH solver needs a free license string. Copy code/model/path_license.txt.example to code/model/path_license.txt and replace the placeholder line with the “Variable value” string from https://pages.cs.wisc.edu/~ferris/path/LICENSE. The runner checks the file at every start and stops with a message if it is missing or still holds the placeholder.

title: Walkthrough: from install to results
section: 3. Test the installation: run the baseline package (no shock)
text:
3. Test the installation: run the baseline package (no shock)
This run tests the installation and nothing else. The baseline input package data/packages/baseline_2025_Input.zip is built by the R pipeline from the USDA 2025 baseline, and its data_shocks.csv holds neutral values (all zeros), so the run reproduces the baseline projections and shows no change anywhere. What it demonstrates is that Julia, the solver and the license work.
scripts/run_model_unix.sh
Defaults: input data/packages/baseline_2025_Input.zip, output output/baseline_Output.zip, years 2025:2034. The run takes about two minutes. The terminal shows, for each year, the three market-clearing checks, the PATH iteration log, and the solver and model status; the last lines are
Output package written to: .../output/baseline_Output.zip
Years solved:  2025 2026 2027 2028 2029 2030 2031 2032 2033 2034
Elapsed:       ... s
Unzip the output package, or open it in a file manager, and look at two files:
SCENARIO_SOLVER_LOG.txt starts with a summary followed by the per-year status, then the full console output:
BSAT scenario solver log
Model version:   v2.27 (2026-07-29)
Run finished:    ...
Elapsed seconds: ...
Julia:           1.12.1
Years requested: 2025 2026 2027 2028 2029 2030 2031 2032 2033 2034
Years solved:    2025 2026 2027 2028 2029 2030 2031 2032 2033 2034
Years skipped:   none

Per-year status (from Results_<year>/Solver_Status_Model_<year>.txt):
  2025  Solver status: FEASIBLE_POINT
  2025  Model status: LOCALLY_SOLVED
  ...
Every year should read FEASIBLE_POINT and LOCALLY_SOLVED. A year that the model refused appears as not solved (market-clearing checks failed or solve skipped) and under “Years skipped”; see Troubleshooting.
METADATA.csv carries the fields of the input package’s metadata plus what the run added:
field,value
Author,BSAT team
Description,Baseline scenario
Comments,Neutral shocks: reproduces the USDA baseline
Pipeline build,2026-09-04T14:39:02
Model calibration,<timestamp>
Scenario simulation,<timestamp>
Model version,v2.27 (2026-07-29)
Years requested,2025 2026 2027 2028 2029 2030 2031 2032 2033 2034
Years solved,2025 2026 2027 2028 2029 2030 2031 2032 2033 2034
The dashboard shows this table for each uploaded package, so the Description line is what identifies a scenario later. The other five files of the package are described in Package and file format. A copy of this baseline output is committed as data/outputs/baseline_2025_Output.zip.
This output is not needed later. Every output package carries the baseline it was solved against (data_targets_adjusted.csv), so the dashboard shows a shock against the baseline from the shock’s own output package alone. The dashboard’s two upload slots are for comparing two different shocks with each other, not a shock against the baseline.

title: Walkthrough: from install to results
section: 4. Three ways to define a scenario
text:
4. Three ways to define a scenario
A scenario is the baseline input package with data_shocks.csv edited. There are three routes to that package; they produce the same file and can be mixed.



Route
Where the shock is written
Best for




Edited CSV plus one command (section 5)
a spreadsheet: a copy of data/scenarios/shocks_template.csv, or a small file listing only the rows to change
several attributes, regions, years or ramps at once; no command-line options to remember; the run starts from the same command


make_shock.jl (section 6)
command-line options: one attribute, a value, and a selection of regions, commodities and years
a single uniform shock; scripting; layering shocks on an existing package


The Julia API (build_scenario, make_shock, run_bsat; Julia reference)
Julia code
loops over many scenarios, or embedding the model in a larger workflow



Whatever the route, the package then goes through the model (run_model.jl or the run scripts) and the dashboard as in sections 6 and 7. The CSV route runs the model itself.

title: Walkthrough: from install to results
text:
5. Scenario from an edited CSV
The shocks file has five columns that matter: region, year, commodity, attribute and value. data/scenarios/README.md documents the ten attributes, their units and neutral value, and the region and commodity codes. Two forms of CSV are accepted:

a full copy of data/scenarios/shocks_template.csv (the baseline shocks, 28,980 rows, all zeros) with some values edited: open it in a spreadsheet, filter by attribute, region, commodity and year, type the values, save as CSV;
a partial file with only the rows to change. Rows absent from the file keep the baseline value.

The China soybean import tariff of the worked example (+10 percentage points from 2026 to 2034) as a partial file, data/scenarios/example_china_soybean_tariff.csv:
region,year,commodity,attribute,value
CHN,2026,Soybean,shock_import_tariff,0.1
CHN,2027,Soybean,shock_import_tariff,0.1
...
CHN,2034,Soybean,shock_import_tariff,0.1
One command builds the package, prints what differs from the baseline, runs the model and writes the output:
scripts/run_scenario_unix.sh data/scenarios/example_china_soybean_tariff.csv \
      output/china_soybean_tariff_Output.zip "China soybean import tariff +10 pp from 2026"
9 row(s) differ from baseline_2025_Input.zip:
  shock_import_tariff                         CHN  Soybean  2026:2034 = 0.1
Input package written to: .../output/china_soybean_tariff_Input.zip (9 row(s) applied, 0 skipped, 9 differ from the template)
... (the model run, as in section 3)
Years solved:  2025 2026 2027 2028 2029 2030 2031 2032 2033 2034
The second argument (output package) defaults to output/<csv name>_Output.zip, the third (description written to METADATA.csv) to Scenario from <csv name>. The input package is written beside the output with the same stem, so a run always leaves both packages behind. On Windows, scripts\run_scenario_windows.bat takes the same arguments.
Rows the command cannot apply are skipped with a warning naming the line and the reason (unknown attribute, region or commodity, a year outside 2025 to 2034, a blank or non-numeric value, a commodity on a region-level attribute, a region and commodity pair the model does not have); the run continues with the other rows and stops only if none can be applied. Header names and codes are matched regardless of case, and the byte-order mark, CRLF line ends and number spellings such as 2026.0 or 1E-1 that spreadsheets produce are accepted. The package’s shocks file is regenerated from the template, so the spreadsheet’s formatting never reaches the model.
To check a CSV without running the model, use the Julia entry point with --build-only; it writes the input package and prints the changes, and --years, --template and --license are also available there (Command line):
julia --project=code/model code/model/run_scenario.jl --shocks my_case.csv --build-only

title: Walkthrough: from install to results
section: 6. Create a shock package with make_shock.jl and simulate it
text:
6. Create a shock package with make_shock.jl and simulate it
code/model/make_shock.jl takes a template package, edits data_shocks.csv for one attribute over a selection of regions, commodities and years, and writes a new package. Start by listing the attributes:
julia --project=code/model code/model/make_shock.jl --list
shock_import_tariff                          [RYNC]  ad valorem import tariff, added in decimal form (0.10 = +10 percentage points)
shock_export_tax                             [RYNC]  ad valorem export tax, added in decimal form
shock_nontariff_import                       [RYNC]  ad valorem equivalent of import non-tariff measures, added in decimal form
shock_nontax_export                          [RYNC]  ad valorem equivalent of export non-tax measures, added in decimal form
shock_land_prod                              [RYNC]  land productivity shifter, decimal change (-0.10 = 10 percent lower yields per hectare)
shock TFP Productivity Value Added           [RYNC]  total factor productivity shifter in value added, decimal change
shock TFP Productivity Intermediates         [RYNC]  total factor productivity shifter in intermediate use (soybean crushing), decimal change
shock_TFP_Productivity_Feed_Use_livestock    [RYNC]  total factor productivity shifter in feed use of livestock, decimal change
shock_land_supply                            [RY]  land supply availability, decimal change (-0.10 = 10 percent less land), region level
shock_ag_expenditure_share                   [RY]  agricultural expenditure share, proportional change (0.05 = 5 percent higher), region level
RYNC attributes vary by region, year and commodity; RY attributes are region-level and ignore --commodities. Two attribute names contain spaces and must be quoted on the command line.

Worked example: China soybean import tariff
Raise China’s ad valorem import tariff on soybeans by 10 percentage points from 2026 to the end of the horizon:
julia --project=code/model code/model/make_shock.jl \
      --template data/packages/baseline_2025_Input.zip \
      --inputpkg output/china_soybean_tariff_Input.zip \
      --shock shock_import_tariff --value 0.10 \
      --regions CHN --commodities Soybean --years 2026:2034 \
      --description "China soybean import tariff +10 pp from 2026"
Wrote .../output/china_soybean_tariff_Input.zip: 9 rows of "shock_import_tariff" set to 0.1
Nine rows changed: one per year from 2026 to 2034. The new package is identical to the template except for those nine values in data_shocks.csv and the Description and Comments fields of METADATA.csv. The package produced by this exact command is committed as data/packages/example_china_soybean_tariff_Input.zip, and its output as data/outputs/example_china_soybean_tariff_Output.zip, so the run below and the dashboard of section 7 can be checked against them. It is the same package that section 5 builds from the CSV.
Options: --regions and --commodities take comma-separated codes (ISO-3 region codes and the commodity codes Barley, Beef, Corn, Cotton, Pork, Poultry, Rice, Sorghum, SoyMeal, SoyOil, Soybean, Wheat); --years takes a range 2026:2034 or a list 2026,2027; omitting a selection means “all”. --add adds the value to what is already in the file instead of replacing it. The command errors if no row matches the selection or if the attribute name is unknown.


Simulate it
scripts/run_model_unix.sh output/china_soybean_tariff_Input.zip output/china_soybean_tariff_Output.zip
The third argument (years) defaults to 2025:2034. The 2025 solution is identical to the baseline because the shock starts in 2026. Check SCENARIO_SOLVER_LOG.txt as in section 3: ten years solved, none skipped. (The CSV route of section 5 already ran this step.)

title: Walkthrough: from install to results
text:
7. Open the dashboard
In a cloud or container environment (Codespaces, Docker), use the hosted dashboard at https://huggingface.co/spaces/bsat-team/BSAT_Viz. Download output/china_soybean_tariff_Output.zip from the codespace to your own computer first: right-click the file in the Explorer panel on the left and choose “Download…”, or drag it from the Explorer onto your desktop. Then upload it on the hosted page. This route needs nothing installed and is the recommended one for everyone; from a local install the hosted copy works the same way, with the file already on your computer.
Run the dashboard server yourself only if both hold: you work on your own computer, not in the cloud, and you want the server on that computer. It needs the optional bsat-dashboard environment from the bootstrap.
scripts/run_dashboard_unix.sh
On Windows the script is scripts\run_dashboard_windows.bat. Either way, open http://localhost:8501 afterwards. Dashboard describes both routes in full.
Upload output/china_soybean_tariff_Output.zip as Shock 1 (up to 20 MB) and leave Shock 2 empty. The baseline output is never uploaded: every package carries its own baseline (data_targets_adjusted.csv) and solution (data_solution.csv), and the dashboard joins them by region, commodity, year and attribute and computes the ratio solution over baseline. The second slot takes a second, different shock, compared against the first; both scenarios are then measured against the baseline of Shock 1, and if the second package’s baseline differs, a warning says so.
What to look at, top to bottom:

Metadata: the Description confirms which package this is.
Time series for China, Soybean, Imports: the baseline path and the scenario path, which diverge from 2026.
Regional changes and Heatmap of changes for Soybean and 2026: the cross-region pattern of the percent change. The year dropdowns open on 2026 because 2025 reproduces the observed data and shows no change.
Top Regional Changes for Soybean, Imports, 2026: which regions’ soybean imports move most.
Table: Scenario Variables, active shocks only: the nine shock_import_tariff rows for China, soybeans.

With a second package loaded, the regional charts show the two scenarios side by side, and a radio button picks the one drawn in the heatmap, on a color scale shared by both.
The attribute names in the dashboard are the display names of the baseline file (Production, Imports, Beginning Stocks, …); the solution file uses lowercase codes that the dashboard maps to them (table in Package and file format).

title: Walkthrough: from install to results
section: 8. Layering shocks and editing data_shocks.csv by hand
text:
8. Layering shocks and editing data_shocks.csv by hand
Layering with make_shock. Run the command again with the previous package as template. Each call edits one attribute; --add accumulates on rows that already hold a value:
julia --project=code/model code/model/make_shock.jl \
      --template output/china_soybean_tariff_Input.zip \
      --inputpkg output/china_soybean_tariff_and_us_land_Input.zip \
      --shock shock_land_supply --value -0.05 --regions USA --years 2026:2034 \
      --description "China soybean tariff +10 pp and US land supply -5 percent from 2026"
Editing by hand. The CSV route of section 5 is the easy form of this: it takes the edited file and does the packaging. Doing it without the command, data_shocks.csv inside the package (folder Input/) is a plain CSV in the standard 13-column schema; open it in a spreadsheet or a script, edit the value column, and zip the folder again (the runner matches files by name, with or without the Input/ folder). The columns are:







Column
Content for a shock row




region
ISO-3 region code (USA, CHN, EUR, …)


year
2025 to 2034


nest
commodity nest (Cereals, Livestock, …); blank for region-level shocks


commodity
commodity code; blank for region-level shocks


input
blank


attribute
one of the ten shock attributes, spelled exactly as in --list


value
the shock, decimal form; 0 is neutral


unit
decimal form


attribute_type
RYNC or RY


attribute_description, region_name, nest_name, commodity_name
labels, not read by the model



Semantics: the model reads the shock rows of the year being solved and adds each value to the baseline level of the corresponding exogenous variable (tariff, export tax, non-tariff measures, land productivity, the three TFP shifters, land supply). The expenditure share is the one exception: the baseline share is multiplied by 1 + value. A value of 0 leaves the baseline unchanged, which is why the file shipped with the baseline package is all zeros. Do not add or remove rows: the scaffold covers every region, commodity and year the model expects, and the ten attribute names must not be changed. Change Description in METADATA.csv so the dashboard can tell the scenario apart.

title: Walkthrough: from install to results
text:
9. Stylized cases
The model team defined four stylized cases for the working paper (BSAT working paper, forthcoming). They are shipped as ready-to-run packages under data/packages/ with their model outputs under data/outputs/, so you can upload a case output on its own, or beside another case as Shock 2, in the dashboard without running anything. Each case is shipped twice: as a partial CSV under data/scenarios/ (the scenario definition, a few rows), and as the make_shock.jl command that produces the same package. Either rebuilds the package from the baseline; solving a case takes about two minutes. From the CSV:
scripts/run_scenario_unix.sh data/scenarios/case1_land_supply_ukraine.csv output/case1_Output.zip \
      "Case 1, land availability: Ukraine land supply 20 percent lower in 2026"
2025 is the realized base year and stays at the baseline in every case: the single-year shocks are placed in 2026, the second year of the horizon, and the nine-step ramps run over 2026 to 2034. Every year is solved independently, so a single-year shock changes only that year’s results.

Case 1: land availability
Ukraine’s land supply is 20 percent lower in 2026 (shock_land_supply, region level).
julia --project=code/model code/model/make_shock.jl --template data/packages/baseline_2025_Input.zip \
      --inputpkg output/case1_Input.zip --shock shock_land_supply --value -0.20 --regions UKR --years 2026 \
      --description "Case 1, land availability: Ukraine land supply 20 percent lower in 2026"
CSV: data/scenarios/case1_land_supply_ukraine.csv. Package: data/packages/case1_land_supply_ukraine_Input.zip. What to look at: Ukrainian area and production of every crop in 2026, and the export flows of wheat and corn.


Case 2: export tax
India applies an export tax of 50 percentage points on rice and wheat in 2026 (shock_export_tax).
julia --project=code/model code/model/make_shock.jl --template data/packages/baseline_2025_Input.zip \
      --inputpkg output/case2_Input.zip --shock shock_export_tax --value 0.50 --regions IND --commodities Rice,Wheat --years 2026 \
      --description "Case 2, export tax: India rice and wheat export tax +50 percentage points in 2026"
CSV: data/scenarios/case2_export_tax_india.csv. Package: data/packages/case2_export_tax_india_Input.zip. What to look at: Indian rice and wheat exports in 2026 and the exports of the other rice exporters (Thailand, Vietnam, Pakistan, United States).


Case 3: TFP improvement
Total factor productivity in the value added of Chinese soybean production rises gradually over the horizon (shock TFP Productivity Value Added). Two variants ship: Case 3a rises 1 percent per year from 1 percent in 2026 to 9 percent in 2034; Case 3b rises 0.5 percent per year from 0.5 to 4.5 percent. 2025 is not shocked, so its results equal the baseline. A ramp is a sequence of make_shock.jl calls, each using the package written by the previous call as template:
# julia --project=code/model
include("code/model/src/BSATRunner.jl"); using .BSATRunner
pkg = "data/packages/baseline_2025_Input.zip"
for (k, y) in enumerate(2026:2034)
    pkg = make_shock(pkg, "output/case3a_Input.zip"; attribute="shock TFP Productivity Value Added",
                     value=0.01k, regions=["CHN"], commodities=["Soybean"], years=[y],
                     description="Case 3a, TFP improvement: China soybean value-added TFP rising 1 to 9 percent over 2026 to 2034").inputpkg_zip
end
For Case 3b use value=0.005k. From the command line, the same ramp is nine make_shock.jl calls, each with the package written by the previous call as --template and --years set to one year.
CSVs: data/scenarios/case3a_tfp_soybean_china.csv, data/scenarios/case3b_tfp_soybean_china_half.csv (nine rows each, one per year from 2026: the ramp is plain to read there). Packages: data/packages/case3a_tfp_soybean_china_Input.zip, data/packages/case3b_tfp_soybean_china_half_Input.zip. What to look at: Chinese soybean production, imports and crushing year by year, and Brazilian and US soybean exports.


Case 4: land productivity decline
Land productivity of US corn and soybeans falls 10 percent in 2026 (shock_land_prod).
julia --project=code/model code/model/make_shock.jl --template data/packages/baseline_2025_Input.zip \
      --inputpkg output/case4_Input.zip --shock shock_land_prod --value -0.10 --regions USA --commodities Corn,Soybean --years 2026 \
      --description "Case 4, land productivity decline: US corn and soybean land productivity 10 percent lower in 2026"
CSV: data/scenarios/case4_land_productivity_usa.csv. Package: data/packages/case4_land_productivity_usa_Input.zip. What to look at: US corn and soybean production, area, yields and exports in 2026, and the imports of the main buyers.
Each case follows the pattern of sections 5 to 7: build and run it from the CSV with scripts/run_scenario_unix.sh, or build it with make_shock.jl and run it with scripts/run_model_unix.sh <Input.zip> <Output.zip>, then open the output in the dashboard.

title: R reference: pipeline scripts
text: One entry per script in code/processing/R/, taken from the header block at the top of each file (Purpose, Reads, Writes, Depends, Notes), which is the authoritative description. Paths under “Reads” and “Writes” are relative to the data root (<repo>/data, or BSAT_DATA_DIR). main.R sources the scripts in numeric order; every script starts with rm(list = ls()) and communicates with the others only through files. How the scripts fit together is in Processing pipeline; how to bring in a new data vintage is in Updating raw data.

title: R reference: pipeline scripts
text:
main.R

Purpose: run the full data-processing pipeline for the 2025-2034 period. Produces the four model-input files in processed/ (data_targets, data_exogenous, data_shocks, data_params_init) and the baseline package.
Run: Rscript main.R from code/processing/, or the run scripts. Sets its working directory to its own folder (through rstudioapi in RStudio, or the --file= argument under Rscript).
Data root: BSAT_DATA_DIR if set, else <repo>/data; stored in the option bsat.data_dir; interim/ and processed/ are created.
Order: 00 01 10 11 12 20 21 [22] [23] 24 30 40 50 60. Script 23 runs only when both large raw files are present; otherwise the shipped interim NTM results are reused, and without those the run stops.

title: R reference: pipeline scripts
text:
00_load_packages.R

Purpose: check that every package the pipeline uses is installed and attach it; nothing is installed. Sourced first by main.R; later scripts clear objects but keep the attached packages. A missing or broken package stops the run with its name.
Reads: none.
Writes: none.
Depends: dplyr, tidyr, stringr, readr, readxl, openxlsx, zip, data.table, lfe, ggplot2 (from setup/environment.yml)
Notes: stringr, data.table and ggplot2 are loaded but no numbered script currently calls them; lfe is used only by 23.

title: R reference: pipeline scripts
text:
01_check_region_commodity_coverage.R

Purpose: expand the region-commodity list of the USDA baseline to the full region x commodity grid and flag the pairs the baseline does not cover.
Reads: raw/region_commodity_list_2025.xlsx (sheet Sheet1: columns region, commodity).
Writes: interim/region_commodity_coverage.csv.
Depends: openxlsx, dplyr, tidyr, readr.
Notes: audit only; no later script reads the output.

title: R reference: pipeline scripts
text:
10_read_baseline_data.R

Purpose: read the commodity sheets of the USDA International Long-Term Projections workbook and reshape them into one long table (commodity x region x year) holding the baseline variables.
Reads: raw/2025 International Long-Term Projections to 2034.xlsx (one sheet per commodity, named as in the commodity list); raw/region_commodity_list_2025.xlsx (sheet Sheet1: region order within each sheet).
Writes: interim/baseline_projections_long.csv.
Depends: openxlsx, dplyr, readr.
Notes: source vintage constant baseline_data <- "2025 International Long-Term Projections to 2034.xlsx". The sheet layout is hard-coded: each region block is 25 rows apart and 21 rows tall, starting at row 9 (Poultry) or row 7 (all other commodities); the number and meaning of the columns per commodity group (CL1 to CL8) is fixed in the script; the regions of a sheet are those of the region list, in order, followed by World. The string -- marks missing values; crop years 2025/26 keep the first year.

title: R reference: pipeline scripts
text:
11_compute_feed_use_decomposition.R

Purpose: split each region’s total feed use of every feed crop across the three livestock products (beef, pork, poultry) in proportion to FAOSTAT livestock value-of-production shares.
Reads: raw/mapping.csv; raw/FAOSTAT_total_livestock_value_constant_IntlD.csv (2015 total livestock value, constant 2014-2016 I$); raw/FAOSTAT_each_livestock_value_constant_IntlD.csv (2015 value by livestock item, indigenous meat); interim/baseline_projections_long.csv (from 10).
Writes: interim/livestock_value_shares.xlsx; interim/feed_use_decomposition.xlsx.
Depends: dplyr, tidyr, readr, openxlsx.
Notes: Z_k = feed_only + ind_feed_other + feed_seed_waste for Barley, Corn, Sorghum, Soybeans, Soybean meal, Soybean oil and Wheat; Z_ik = Z_k x value share of livestock i. A missing value share is read as no demand (set to 0). FAOSTAT column Area Code (ISO3) and the five (indigenous) Item labels are matched by name; Myanmar is recoded MMR to BUR. Only group A regions and years from 2025 are kept.

title: R reference: pipeline scripts
text:
12_generate_data_targets.R

Purpose: build data_targets.csv, the baseline levels the model is calibrated to, from the long baseline table and the feed-use decomposition.
Reads: interim/baseline_projections_long.csv (from 10); interim/feed_use_decomposition.xlsx (from 11); raw/mapping.csv; raw/baseline_units.csv (unit per commodity x attribute_description).
Writes: processed/data_targets.csv (overwritten afterwards by 50).
Depends: dplyr, tidyr, readr, readxl.
Notes: lst_obsv_yr <- 2025 is the first year of the analysis period; keep it equal to first_yr in 30. Commodities are renamed to model codes (Beef, SoyMeal, SoyOil, Soybean) and assigned to nests. Soybean-market consistency check: when a region has SoyOil or SoyMeal projections but no soybean market, SoyOil in BGD is reallocated to OAO and SoyOil and SoyMeal in ECO to ONA (see the long note in the script). All quantity attributes are rounded to whole units; yields and extraction rates are not (13 re-derives them).

title: R reference: pipeline scripts
text:
20_compute_ag_expenditure_share.R

Purpose: compute the agricultural expenditure share (spending on the twelve modeled commodities as a percentage of real GDP) by region for 2025, and save the annual international price series built along the way.
Reads: processed/data_targets.csv (from 12, before harmonization: food and feed quantities); raw/2026-06-19 IMF Commodity Prices external-data.xlsx (sheet External: monthly, nine non-meat commodities); raw/2026-06-19 International Prices FAO Meat.xlsx (sheet data: monthly export prices, beef, pork, poultry); raw/2026-06-24 CPI_US.xlsx (sheet Sheet1: columns year, CPI_2017); raw/Global GDP Shares and GDP Growth Assumptions to 2035.xlsx (first sheet: USDA real GDP levels and growth); raw/mapping.csv.
Writes: interim/international_prices_annual.csv (marketing-year averages, native units, all years); interim/ag_expenditure_shares.csv.
Depends: openxlsx, dplyr, tidyr, readr.
Notes: IMF series are picked by the code in row 1 (imf_meta: PBARL, PWHEAMT, PCOTTIND, PRICENPQ, PMAIZMT, PSORG, PSOYB, PSMEA, PSOIL); dates are the YYYYMm labels in column 1. FAO meat prices are simple averages of fixed column positions (columns 3-5 beef, 6/8/9 pork, 7/10 poultry; dates MM/DD/YYYY in column 2). Prices are deflated to 2017 USD with CPI_2017 and averaged over USDA marketing years (start_mo); an incomplete last year uses the last 12 observed months. The GDP workbook is read by position (column 2 = 2025 level, columns 6-10 = growth 2025-2029, column 13 = 2026-35 average) and its region labels must match xwalk plus the OAO and ONA residual definitions. Only year 2025 is exported.

21_compute_land_cost_share.R

Purpose: compute the land cost share of value added (phi_f) for every region and crop from U.S. per-acre variable costs, relative yields and the USDA international TFP land cost shares.
Reads: raw/AgTFPInternational2023.xlsx (sheet Cost Shares, rows 3-182, columns 3 and 33: ISO3, 2021-2030); raw/variable_costs_2025/*to 2035*.xlsx (five USDA cost-of-production workbooks); raw/mapping.csv; interim/baseline_projections_long.csv (from 10: area and yield by region and crop).
Writes: interim/variable_costs_us_2025.csv (extracted U.S. per-acre variable costs, long); interim/region_commodity_land_cost_shares.csv.
Depends: openxlsx, dplyr, readr.
Notes: vintage constants: vc_pattern <- "to 2035" selects the cost workbooks in raw/variable_costs_2025/; the land-share column is renamed from its header 2021-2030. The EUR land share is hard-coded at 0.113. Cost workbooks are parsed by row label: Table ... U.S. <crop>, an Item header row with the crop years, Variable costs of production and the following Per acre row. Land rents solve w * sum_k s_rk / (H_rk + w) = land share with uniroot on [0, 1000]; shares are winsorized at the 5th and 95th percentiles within each year. Years from 2025 are exported. The derivation is in data/land cost share.md.

text:
22_compute_tariff_ave.R

Purpose: compute region-commodity ad valorem import tariffs (simple average of WITS MFN tariffs, latest reported year per product) and a zero export-tax scaffold.
Reads: raw/trade_barriers/tariff_ave_WITS_2023.csv (WITS TRAINS export: Reporter, Product, DutyType, Simple Average, Tariff Year); raw/trade_barriers/country_code_WITS.xlsx (columns country, ISO3, Reporter); raw/mapping.csv.

Depends: openxlsx, dplyr, tidyr, readr.
Notes: HS codes are mapped to commodities by fixed 4- and 6-digit lists (0201, 0202, 0207, 1001, 1003, 1005, 1006, 1007, 1201, 1507, 2304, 5201-5203, …). Missing tariffs are set to 0 (with the current data: all of Iraq, Saudi Arabia pork, Pakistan soybean oil). The EU is one reporter (EUN). Export taxes are not observed and are 0 everywhere. The year column of the tariff output is the string 2023 (or last observed).

title: R reference: pipeline scripts
text:
23_compute_NTM_ave.R

Purpose: estimate a model of non-tariff-measure ad valorem equivalents (AVE) on tariffs, GDP per capita and agricultural imports with region x product fixed effects, impute missing AVEs, and aggregate them into GDP-weighted region-commodity import NTMs; export NTMs are a zero scaffold.
Reads: raw/trade_barriers/ave_hs_importer.csv (World Bank NTM AVEs: importer, hs2code, ave1C, ave2C); raw/trade_barriers/BACI_HS92_Y2014_V202401b.csv (CEPII bilateral flows 2014: t, i, j, k, v, q; large, not in the repository); raw/trade_barriers/country_codes_V202401b.csv (BACI numeric code to country_iso3); raw/trade_barriers/ag_hs_products.csv (agricultural HS product list, column Product); raw/trade_barriers/ag_tariff_USA_2014.xls (sheet Applied_MFN, column E from row 6: HS6 codes); raw/trade_barriers/tariff_ave_2014_WITS.csv (WITS 2014 tariff AVEs; large, not in the repository); raw/trade_barriers/country_code_WITS.xlsx (Reporter to ISO3); raw/trade_barriers/country_region_WB.xlsx (sheet List of economies, rows 1-219, columns 2-3: Code, Region); raw/current_GDPpc_2014_WB.csv and raw/current_GDP_2014_WB.csv (World Bank, column 2014 [YR2014]); raw/current_GDPpc_IMF.xls and raw/current_GDP_IMF.xls (IMF WEO, Taiwan only); raw/mapping.csv.
Writes: interim/model_estimates.RData (rxp_fe and the four beta coefficients); interim/NTM_regression_results.csv (coefficients, standard errors and fit statistics); interim/NTM_regression_table.tex (the same results as a LaTeX table for the paper); interim/NTM_ave_imputed.RData (NTM_ave_imputed: country x commodity actual and imputed AVE); interim/NTM_IMP_ave_region.csv; interim/NTM_EXP_ave_region.csv.
Depends: dplyr, tidyr, readr, readxl, openxlsx, lfe.
Notes: sourced by main.R only when both large raw files are present; otherwise the two interim CSVs are reused. Regression: ave ~ AVE_Tariff + AVE_Tariff_ag + log_GDPpc + log_total_imp_ag | region_geo:product_id (felm). Negative imputations are set to 0; gaps for Barley, Sorghum, Soybeans and Wheat take the country’s Corn, Rice and Cotton average; Iraq takes its geographic-region average. EU members plus GBR are pooled as EUN; Myanmar MMR to BUR; Taiwan is BACI code 490. World Bank regions are merged into Euro-MENA and Asia-Pacific for the fixed effects. Reference year of all inputs is 2014. Diagnostics: 25. The regression is described in data/impute_ave_NTM.R.md.

title: R reference: pipeline scripts
text:
30_generate_data_shocks.R

Purpose: generate data_shocks.csv, a zero-filled scaffold of every shock attribute for each region, commodity and year of the analysis period. Levels live in data_exogenous.csv; this file holds the deviations.
Reads: raw/mapping.csv (the 42 model regions).
Writes: processed/data_shocks.csv.
Depends: dplyr, tidyr, readr, tibble.
Notes: first_yr <- 2025 and last_yr <- 2034 define the horizon; keep first_yr equal to lst_obsv_yr in 12. Ten shock attributes: four trade barriers (all commodities), TFP value added and land productivity (crops), TFP feed use (livestock), TFP intermediates (SoyMeal, SoyOil), and two region-level shocks (ag expenditure share, land supply). Two attribute names contain spaces. Editing these values is how counterfactual scenarios are defined.

Purpose: generate data_params_init.csv, the initial values of the seven commodity-level substitution and transformation elasticities.
Reads: none.
Writes: processed/data_params_init.csv.
Depends: dplyr, readr.
Notes: values are hard-coded: sigma_d 3.8 (12 commodities), sigma_f 1.1 (7 crops), sigma_c 5 (SoyMeal, SoyOil), sigma_l 0.25, sigma_z 0.5 and sigma_w 3.8 (livestock), omega_s 5 (12 commodities); 42 rows with attribute type C.

title: R reference: pipeline scripts
text:
50_harmonize_targets.R

Purpose: apply to the rounded targets of 12 the same three adjustments the model would make on its own, in the model’s order, so that the model finds no residual to repair and the neutral run reproduces every target exactly.
Reads: processed/data_targets.csv (written by 12).
Writes: processed/data_targets.csv (overwritten, harmonized); interim/harmonization_log.csv (columns region, year, commodity, check (consumption or market), residual, adjusted (the attribute changed), delta, status).
Depends: dplyr, tidyr, readr.
Notes: COTTON_KG_PER_BALE <- 217.728111162486 is the model’s bale-to-kg factor. Three adjustments, all logged, in the model’s order. (a) Consumption: a residual TC - (FOOD + LIV + OTR + CRSH) within plus or minus 2 is added to the largest of those four components, the first maximum in that order; when the largest is feed to livestock or other feed, the rows are left alone and the residual is left to the model (status left to the model: feed component), because the model repairs it in its internal feed totals but reports feed consumption from the unrepaired target (df_DCFEED1 in model_core.jl). (b) Market: a residual of BS + Q + M - Loss = TC + X + ES within plus or minus 2 is subtracted from the largest of beginning stocks, production and imports, the first maximum in that order. (c) Derived series: yields as production over area (cotton in kg per hectare) and extraction rates as 100 times production over soybean crushing, both computed from the adjusted values. Residuals outside plus or minus 2 are not adjusted; they are logged with a status containing outside the model's ±2 window and raise a warning(), and the model refuses that year.

Purpose: bundle the four processed CSV files and a METADATA.csv into the standard model input package (a zip with an Input/ folder) specified in Package and file format. The shocks file holds neutral values, so the package is the baseline package.
Reads: processed/data_params_init.csv; processed/data_exogenous.csv; processed/data_targets.csv; processed/data_shocks.csv.
Writes: packages/baseline_<first year>_Input.zip (first year = smallest year in data_targets.csv).
Depends: readr, dplyr, zip, tibble.
Notes: METADATA.csv records Author, Description, Comments and the build timestamp (Pipeline build). An existing zip with the same name is replaced.

title: Julia reference: BSATRunner
text:
BSATRunner (code/model/src/BSATRunner.jl) wraps the verbatim model core. It reads a standard input package, runs the model year by year and writes a standard output package. Entry points: run_bsat from Julia, run_model.jl from the command line, and run_scenario.jl for the edited-CSV route (Command line). All wrapper names are prefixed bsat_ so they cannot collide with variables assigned inside the model core, which is evaluated in the module’s global scope.
Load the module from the repository root:
Exports: run_bsat, make_shock, build_scenario, BSAT_SHOCKS.

text:
Exported functions

run_bsat
run_bsat(input_zip; output_zip="Output.zip", periods=2025:2034, workdir=nothing,
         keep_workdir=false, license=BSAT_DEFAULT_LICENSE)
Run the BSAT model on the input package input_zip for the years in periods and write the output package to output_zip.
Arguments:

input_zip::AbstractString: path of the input package.
output_zip::AbstractString: path of the output package to write (folders are created).
periods: years to simulate; any collection of integers.
workdir: folder in which the core reads Input/ and writes its per-year files. Defaults to a fresh temporary folder, deleted afterwards unless keep_workdir=true.
keep_workdir::Bool: keep the working folder.
license::AbstractString: path of the PATH license file.

Returns a named tuple with output_zip, periods_solved, periods_skipped, elapsed (seconds) and workdir (nothing when the temporary folder was deleted).
Years the model refuses (market-clearing checks fail, or the solver does not reach a solution) are skipped by the core and reported in SCENARIO_SOLVER_LOG.txt and in the return value; the remaining years still produce output. Errors if periods is empty, the license file is missing or holds the placeholder, or the input package lacks one of the four required files. Warns when no year was solved.


make_shock
make_shock(template_zip, inputpkg_zip; attribute, value, regions=nothing, commodities=nothing,
           years=nothing, mode=:set, description=nothing)
Create a scenario input package from template_zip by editing data_shocks.csv.
Arguments:

template_zip::AbstractString, inputpkg_zip::AbstractString: packages to read and write; the package written is a scenario input package, the input of run_bsat.
attribute::AbstractString: one of the ten shock attributes (see BSAT_SHOCKS).
value::Real: the shock in decimal form.
regions, commodities, years: optional selections (vectors of ISO-3 codes, commodity codes, integer years). nothing selects every row of that attribute. Region-level shocks ignore commodities.
mode::Symbol: :set writes value; :add adds it to the existing value, which lets shocks be layered by calling the function repeatedly with the previous package as template.
description: replaces the Description field of METADATA.csv (created if the template has no metadata file) and records the derivation in Comments, so the dashboard shows what the scenario is.

Returns (inputpkg_zip, rows_changed, attribute, value). Errors if the attribute is unknown, mode is not :set or :add, the template has no data_shocks.csv, or no row matches the selection.


build_scenario
build_scenario(template_zip, shocks_csv, inputpkg_zip; description=nothing, io=stdout)
Create a scenario input package from template_zip by writing the values of shocks_csv into its data_shocks.csv. The CSV can be a full edited copy of the shocks file or only the rows to change; rows are matched on region, year, commodity and attribute, and rows absent from the CSV keep the template value. The package’s shocks file is regenerated from the template table, so the spreadsheet’s formatting never reaches the model.
Arguments:

template_zip::AbstractString, shocks_csv::AbstractString, inputpkg_zip::AbstractString: package to read, CSV to apply, scenario input package to write.
description: written to the Description field of METADATA.csv; default Scenario from <csv name>. The Comments field records the source CSV and the count of changed rows.
io::IO: where the changed rows are printed, grouped by attribute, region and commodity (devnull to silence).

Only the columns region, year, commodity, attribute and value are read; header names and codes are matched regardless of case and surrounding blanks. A row that cannot be applied (unknown attribute, region or commodity; a commodity on a region-level attribute or none on a commodity-level one; a year outside the template; a blank or non-numeric value; a region and commodity pair the template does not have) is reported with @warn (one warning per reason, with line numbers) and skipped; a repeated key warns and the last row wins. Errors if the template has no data_shocks.csv, a required column is missing, or no row can be applied; warns if the result equals the template.
Returns (inputpkg_zip, rows_read, rows_applied, rows_skipped, rows_changed, changes), where changes is a DataFrame (attribute, region, commodity, year, value) of the rows whose value differs from the template.

title: Model
text: This page describes the BSAT model as implemented in code/model/src/model_core.jl, and the runner that wraps it. It is written from the code, without equations. The economic derivation is in the working paper (BSAT working paper, forthcoming); where the paper and the code differ, the code is the specification. The core file is not edited in this repository: every change to the model is reviewed by the model authors, and the regression test compares the output with archived reference runs.

title: Model
text:
Purpose
BSAT is a multi-region partial-equilibrium model of twelve agricultural commodities. It is calibrated so that, with no shocks, it reproduces the USDA international baseline projections exactly, one year at a time. A scenario changes one or more exogenous variables (tariffs, export taxes, non-tariff measures, land supply, land productivity, total factor productivity, the agricultural expenditure share) and the model reports the new levels of production, consumption, trade, stocks, area, yields and crushing for every region and commodity, next to the baseline levels.
The model is formulated in hat calculus in the calibrated share form: variables are ratios to their baseline values, and the distribution parameters of the nested functional forms are the value shares observed in the baseline. It is solved as a mixed complementarity problem with the PATH solver through JuMP.

title: Model
text:
Sets
The sets are read from the targets file of the year being solved and from fixed lists in the code.

Regions: the 42 countries and aggregate regions of the USDA baseline, identified by ISO-3 style codes (USA, CHN, EUR, OAO, …). The regions covered by each commodity are those the baseline reports; see data/Region_list.txt and data/raw/mapping.csv.
Commodities: twelve, in three groups.

Primary crops (7): Barley, Corn, Cotton, Rice, Sorghum, Soybean, Wheat. Produced from land and a non-land input bundle.
Secondary products (2): SoyMeal, SoyOil. Produced by crushing soybeans, the only intermediate input.
Livestock (3): Beef, Pork, Poultry. Produced from feed and non-feed inputs; the feed crops are Barley, Corn, Sorghum, SoyMeal, SoyOil, Soybean, Wheat.

Nests: eight demand nests grouping the commodities.

title: Model
text:
Inputs
The model reads the four files of an input package (Package and file format). What each contributes:

data_targets.csv: for the year being solved, the baseline levels of beginning stocks, production, imports, total, food and feed consumption, exports, ending stocks, loss, area, crushing, and feed use of each feed crop by each livestock product (Total_feed_use_input_to_commodity). The Yields and Extraction Rate rows are not used: the code derives both series from production, area and crush.
data_exogenous.csv: the elasticities and parameters that are not commodity-level initial values (sigma_t, sigma_u, sigma_n per nest, sigma_a, sigma_i, phi_i, phi_f, omega_q, omega_c, epsilon_l, epsilon_q); international prices; population and GDP per capita; the price normalizations (Price of No Land Input, Price of No AG, P_NO_FEED); livestock inventory and slaughter (inv_liv, slt_liv); and the baseline levels of the shock variables (Ag Expenditure Share, Import tariff, Export tax, the two NTM attributes, Land Productivity, Land Unavailability, the three TFP attributes).
data_params_init.csv: the seven commodity-level elasticities (sigma_d, sigma_f, sigma_c, sigma_l, sigma_z, sigma_w, omega_s).
data_shocks.csv: the ten shock attributes for the year being solved.

title: Model
text:
Calibration
Calibration happens inside the year loop, before the equations are built. The distribution parameters of every nested function (the value shares of domestic and imported goods in food and feed demand, of food, feed, crushing and export in supply, of land within value added, of each feed crop in livestock feed, of stocks and current supply, of each commodity within its nest, and of agriculture within total expenditure) are computed from the targets and the exogenous prices, tariffs and NTMs of that year, so that the baseline is an equilibrium of the model. The elasticities are not estimated here: sigma_t (substitution between agricultural and non-agricultural consumption, 0.0287) and sigma_u (substitution across nests, 0.2747) come from the calibration in the working paper and are entered in data/raw/exogenous_data.csv, from which the pipeline copies them into data_exogenous.csv; sigma_n per nest, sigma_a, sigma_i, phi_i, omega_q, omega_c, epsilon_l and epsilon_q are entered in the same file; the land cost shares phi_f per region, crop and year are computed by pipeline script 21 from U.S. variable costs, relative yields and the USDA international land cost shares (data/land cost share.md) and read for the year being solved; the seven commodity-level elasticities come from data_params_init.csv (values set in pipeline script 40). The output file data_params_calibrated.csv collects the parameters the model used. The livestock feed technology is described in data/Leontief Production Function for Livestock.md.

title: Model
section: The year loop and market-clearing checks
text:
The year loop and market-clearing checks
The core loops over the requested years (default 2025 to 2034). Each year is solved on its own: the targets and shocks of that year are read, the model is calibrated, built and solved, and the results are written. Years do not feed into each other; beginning stocks of a year are its target values.
Before calibrating, the code checks that the targets are internally consistent, in three steps:

Supply and demand per market. For every region and commodity, beginning stocks plus production plus imports minus loss must equal total consumption plus exports plus ending stocks. Residuals within plus or minus 2 (in the units of the targets, thousand metric tons for most commodities) are repaired by the code itself: the residual is subtracted from the largest of beginning stocks, production and imports, the first maximum in that order.
Consumption components. Food consumption, feed consumption (by livestock and other) and crushing must add up to total consumption. Residuals within plus or minus 2 are added to the largest of those components, the first maximum in the order food consumption, feed to livestock, other feed, crushing, on the assumption that the total is the true value. After both repairs the code recomputes the extraction-rate target from the adjusted production and crush. The pipeline’s harmonization step (script 50) applies these same three adjustments, in the same order, before the package is built, and logs each one in data/interim/harmonization_log.csv. Residuals that fall on the feed components are left to the code, which repairs them internally but reports feed consumption from the unrepaired target; the pipeline’s package and the unharmonized targets therefore give the same solution.
Import components. Imports allocated to food, feed, crushing and other uses must add up to total imports.

Each check compares the largest absolute difference across markets with a threshold of 1e-6 and prints All markets: CLEAR or NOT CLEAR. If any check fails, the code prints Baseline Projections Data DO NOT clear in levels and skips the year; the runner records it under “Years skipped”. With the pipeline’s harmonized targets all ten years clear.

title: Model
section: Shocks and how they are applied
text:
Shocks and how they are applied
The ten shock attributes and their units are listed in Package and file format. For the year being solved, the code reads the shock rows and forms the new level of each exogenous variable:

Import tariff, export tax, import and export non-tariff measures, land productivity, TFP in value added, TFP in intermediates and TFP in livestock feed use, and land supply availability: new level = baseline level + shock value (per region and commodity, or per region for land supply).
Agricultural expenditure share: new share = baseline share multiplied by (1 + shock value).

A shock value of 0 leaves the variable at its baseline level. The other exogenous variables (non-land input price, GDP per capita, population, non-agricultural price, non-feed price, beginning stocks) are held at their baseline values in every scenario. The equations then compare the new level with the baseline level; for example, land supply responds to the ratio of new to baseline availability through the land supply elasticity epsilon_l, and value added in a crop responds to the ratio of new to baseline TFP through sigma_i.

title: Model
text:
Solver
The model is a JuMP model with complementarity constraints solved by PATH through PATHSolver.jl. The license string is registered by the runner from code/model/path_license.txt before the first solve. Data preparation uses BigFloat arithmetic at 128-bit precision (setprecision(128)) so that the calibrated shares reproduce the targets exactly.
The solver attributes are set in section 5 of the core file. The ones that determine the outcome:

After optimize!, the code accepts the year when the termination status is OPTIMAL or LOCALLY_SOLVED and the primal status is FEASIBLE_POINT or NEARLY_FEASIBLE_POINT. A TIME_LIMIT termination with a feasible point is accepted with a warning. Any other outcome prints Simulation CANNOT be generated for baseline projections of the year ... and the year is skipped. The status pair is written to Results_<year>/Solver_Status_Model_<year>.txt and copied into the solver log.

title: Model
text:
Outputs and reporting conventions
For each solved year the core writes, in the working folder, Results_<year>/ (solver status and every model variable in All Results.csv) and Output_<year>/ (the per-year data_solution.csv, data_targets.csv, data_params_calibrated.csv, data_exogenous.csv, data_shocks.csv and METADATA.csv). The runner concatenates the per-year solution and target files into the output package (Package and file format).
data_solution.csv holds, per region and commodity, the new levels of beginning stocks (target value), production, imports, total, food and feed consumption, exports, ending stocks, loss, area, crushing, and two derived series:

Yields are production over area. For cotton, production in bales is converted to kilograms with the factor 217.728111162486 kg per bale (the conversion implicit in the USDA baseline), so cotton yields are in kg per hectare. Beef, pork and poultry yields are reported as missing, consistent with USDA data.
Extraction rates are 100 times output over the soybean crush of the region, in percent. The code reports them for soybean meal only (the soybean oil branch of the reporting section is never joined into the output), wherever it has output and crush, including two region-commodity pairs (OAO and ONA for SoyMeal) for which the pipeline has no target. The extraction-rate target is recomputed after the two target repairs, from the adjusted production and crush.

The pipeline’s harmonization step derives yields and extraction rates in the targets with these same conventions, which is why the neutral run reproduces them exactly.

title: Model
text:
Runner architecture
The core file is the year loop of the original model script, copied verbatim. Everything around it lives in the BSATRunner module (code/model/src/BSATRunner.jl, io.jl, run.jl, shocks.jl, scenario.jl):

run_bsat registers the PATH license, sets the BigFloat precision, creates a working folder (a temporary one by default) and extracts the four input files into Input/, matching archive entries by name.
It defines the global periods and evaluates the core file inside the module, with the working folder as current directory, exactly as the original script ran in Main. Standard output, including the C-level output of PATH, is copied to a console log.
It collects the per-year files into Output/, writes METADATA.csv (input metadata plus timestamps, model version, years requested and solved) and SCENARIO_SOLVER_LOG.txt, and zips the seven files at the archive root.

Wrapper names are prefixed bsat_ so they cannot collide with the variables the core assigns in the module’s global scope. run_model.jl is the command-line front end; make_shock derives scenario packages by editing data_shocks.csv, and build_scenario (front end run_scenario.jl) does the same from an edited copy of that file. Signatures are in the Julia reference.

title: Model
text:
Runtime and memory
A run of the baseline package over 2025 to 2034 takes about two minutes and peaks at about 1.6 GB of memory on a workstation. PATH is single-threaded, so more cores do not shorten the run and a laptop gives similar times.

title: Model
text:
Regression test
code/model/test/runtests.jl runs the model on two fixture packages and compares the SHA-256 of every data CSV in the output package with the checksums in code/model/test/expected/:

data/packages/baseline_2025_Input.zip over 2025 to 2034: the package built by the pipeline, the golden reference of this release; the neutral run reproduces every target attribute exactly.
test/fixtures/Input_2025_authors.zip over 2025 to 2034: the model authors’ own input package of July 2026, whose targets are not harmonized, so the model applies its own repairs. Its solution file must be identical to the one of the pipeline’s package, which checks that the pipeline’s harmonization step mirrors the model.

METADATA.csv and SCENARIO_SOLVER_LOG.txt carry timestamps and are checked for presence only. The test also exercises make_shock (row counts, package contents, error cases) and build_scenario (test/test_scenario.jl: partial and full CSVs, spreadsheet spellings, skipped rows, the command-line entry points of run_scenario.jl and make_shock.jl, and that every CSV under data/scenarios/ rebuilds its committed package byte for byte). Run it with
julia --project=code/model code/model/test/runtests.jl
It takes about four minutes. Run it after any change to the wrapper, the packages or the environment.

title: Local installation: Windows
text:
Everything installs under .bsat_local\ inside the repository folder, or under the folder named by the BSAT_LOCAL_DIR environment variable if it is set. Nothing touches the registry, the system PATH or any folder outside the install folder; PATH changes are made inside each batch script and discarded when the window closes.
Disk space: about 4 to 6 GB. First run: 10 to 30 minutes, depending on network speed.
The batch scripts are exercised end to end on a GitHub-hosted Windows runner (.github/workflows/windows-check.yml). Agency laptops add proxies, antivirus and path-length limits that the runner does not have; see Troubleshooting and please report problems.

title: Local installation: Windows
text:
Prerequisites

Windows 10 build 1803 or later (ships curl.exe and PowerShell 5 with Expand-Archive).
No administrator rights.

title: Local installation: Windows
text:
Step 1: get the repository
If you downloaded BSAT as a ZIP file (the green “Code” button on the repository page, then “Download ZIP”), right-click it, choose “Extract All”, and pick a folder whose path has no spaces (for example C:\Users\yourname\bsat). Then open a Command Prompt (Win+R, cmd) and change into it:
cd C:\Users\yourname\bsat
With Git installed:
git clone https://github.com/BSAT-team/BSAT.git
cd bsat

title: Local installation: Windows
text:
Step 2: bootstrap
scripts\bootstrap_windows.bat
The script:

Downloads micromamba.exe (2.8.1) to .bsat_local\bin\.
Creates the bsat conda environment at .bsat_local\envs\bsat from setup\environment.yml (R 4.5 and the pipeline’s R packages). Required. An existing environment with another R version is recreated.
Downloads Julia 1.12.1 to .bsat_local\julia\.
Runs Pkg.instantiate() and Pkg.precompile() for code\model\Project.toml.
Creates the bsat-dashboard conda environment at .bsat_local\envs\bsat-dashboard from setup\environment-dashboard.yml (Python 3.11, pandas, numpy, altair, streamlit). Optional: it is only needed to run the dashboard locally.

The two conda environments are separate on purpose. The model and the pipeline never needed Python; Streamlit pulls in pyarrow and libarrow, a large dependency tree that failed to extract on a locked-down Windows laptop. The bootstrap therefore creates the dashboard environment last, reports a failure there as a warning rather than an error, and finishes with “Bootstrap complete” either way. The hosted dashboard at https://huggingface.co/spaces/bsat-team/BSAT_Viz is the default way to view results, so the environment can be skipped:
scripts\bootstrap_windows.bat --no-dashboard
Each environment is created in a fresh folder (a partial environment from an interrupted run is removed first). If creation fails, the script clears the package cache (micromamba clean -a and .bsat_local\mamba\pkgs) and tries once more, then prints hints. An environment counts as already present when conda-meta\history exists in its folder.
If a required step fails, the script prints Bootstrap FAILED and exits with a non-zero code; see Troubleshooting. Re-running is safe: completed steps are skipped. Do not move or rename the repository folder afterwards (see Troubleshooting).

Choosing the install folder
Windows limits paths to 260 characters unless an administrator enables long paths, and some conda packages unpack into deeply nested folders. If package extraction fails, set BSAT_LOCAL_DIR to a short path in the same window before running the bootstrap; the run scripts read the same variable, so set it in every new window:
set BSAT_LOCAL_DIR=C:\bsat_local
scripts\bootstrap_windows.bat

Step 3: add the PATH solver license

Open https://pages.cs.wisc.edu/~ferris/path/LICENSE and copy the string in the “Variable value” field.
Copy code\model\path_license.txt.example to code\model\path_license.txt (no .example extension).
Open the new file in a text editor and replace the placeholder line with the string. Lines starting with # and blank lines are ignored; the first other line is the license.

The runner stops with a message if the file is missing, holds only comments, or still contains the placeholder.

Runs Rscript main.R from code\processing\ inside the bsat environment. Five raw files are not distributed with the repository; scripts\fetch_large_raw_data.bat reports which are present and, with --download, fetches the CEPII archive. See Raw data sources.

Step 6: run the dashboard locally (optional)
The dashboard is hosted online (Dashboard), which needs nothing installed. The hosted copy is the recommended way to view results and accepts output packages produced locally just as it does any other. The script below is only for running the dashboard server on your own computer; it needs the bsat-dashboard environment (bootstrap without --no-dashboard):
scripts\run_dashboard_windows.bat
The script runs streamlit run app.py from code\visualization\ inside the bsat-dashboard environment. Open http://localhost:8501 in a browser. If the environment is absent, the script says so and prints the hosted URL; rerun the bootstrap to create it.

text:
Notes

The scripts derive the repository path from their own location, so they can be run from any folder.
All scripts honor BSAT_LOCAL_DIR; when it is unset they use .bsat_local\ inside the repository.
To reset the environment completely, delete .bsat_local\ (or the BSAT_LOCAL_DIR folder) and rerun scripts\bootstrap_windows.bat. This does not affect your code, data or path_license.txt.
Shock authoring uses the Julia command line directly; with the portable Julia the command is .bsat_local\julia\bin\julia.exe --project=code\model code\model\make_shock.jl --list.
If you edit a batch script and it stops with ... was unexpected at this time, a parenthesis inside an if block is the usual cause; see Troubleshooting.

title: Cloud and Docker installation
text:
Two options run the same container image, defined in .devcontainer/Dockerfile:
The image contains micromamba, two conda environments and Julia 1.12.1 at /opt/julia. The bsat environment (R 4.5 and the pipeline’s packages, from setup/environment.yml) is installed at /opt/envs/bsat; the bsat-dashboard environment (Python 3.11, pandas, numpy, altair, streamlit, from setup/environment-dashboard.yml) at /opt/envs/bsat-dashboard. title: Cloud and Docker installation
text:
Option A: GitHub Codespaces

What you need

A free account at https://github.com.
A modern browser.
Codespaces quota: free personal accounts receive a monthly allowance of core-hours, enough for several full runs.



Steps

Fork the repository. On the repository page (BSAT-team/BSAT), click “Fork” to create your own copy.
Create a codespace. On your fork, click the green “Code” button, open the “Codespaces” tab, and click “Create codespace on main”. GitHub builds the container and then runs

Install nothing. VS Code offers to install extensions while the codespace opens, and the R extension in particular asks to install the R language server (“languageserver”) and then reports that the installation or the start failed. Decline or close every such prompt and dismiss the error message. The container already has Julia, R and the dashboard environment, and none of the model, the pipeline or the dashboard uses those extensions.
Commands go into the terminal, the panel at the bottom of the window. It is usually open when the codespace starts; if it is closed, open it from the menu with Terminal > New Terminal (the menu is behind the three-line icon at the top left of the browser window) or with the keyboard shortcut Ctrl+` (the backtick key). The prompt already sits in the repository root, so the commands below can be typed as they are and run with Enter.
Add the PATH license. In the integrated terminal:
cp code/model/path_license.txt.example code/model/path_license.txt
Open code/model/path_license.txt in the editor and replace the placeholder line with the string from https://pages.cs.wisc.edu/~ferris/path/LICENSE (the “Variable value” field on that page). The runner refuses to start while the placeholder line is still there.
Run the baseline.
scripts/run_model_unix.sh
This runs data/packages/baseline_2025_Input.zip for 2025 to 2034 and writes output/baseline_Output.zip. Pass other arguments to run a different package: scripts/run_model_unix.sh <Input.zip> <Output.zip> <from:to>.
Optional: rebuild the inputs from raw data.
scripts/run_r_pipeline_unix.sh
The non-tariff-measure step needs two raw files that are not in the repository; see scripts/fetch_large_raw_data.sh and Raw data sources.
View results in the dashboard. Use the hosted copy at https://huggingface.co/spaces/bsat-team/BSAT_Viz. Download the output package from the codespace to your own computer first: find it under output/ in the Explorer panel on the left, right-click it and choose “Download…”, or drag the file from the Explorer onto your desktop. Then upload it on the hosted page. One package is enough, because it carries the baseline it was solved against; a second is uploaded only to compare two different shocks.
Running the dashboard server inside a codespace is not supported. scripts/run_dashboard_unix.sh is for installs on your own computer, where the server and the browser are on the same machine. See Dashboard.



Saving your work
Changes live on the codespace’s disk. To keep them in your fork, commit and push from the terminal:
git add .
git commit -m "my scenario packages"
git push
Closing the browser tab suspends the codespace; resume it from https://github.com/codespaces.

title: Cloud and Docker installation
text:
Option B: Docker
The image uses only public base images and downloads from conda-forge, julialang-s3.julialang.org and github.com. It works on any machine with Docker Engine, including an internal GitHub Enterprise setup without Codespaces.

Build the image
On a machine with Docker and outbound internet access, from the repository root:
docker build -f .devcontainer/Dockerfile -t bsat .
The Julia packages are not part of the image; they are instantiated on first use (below) into a named Docker volume, so they survive when the container is removed.


Run the container
Mount the repository into the container and open a shell:
docker run --rm -it \
  -v "$(pwd):/workspace" \
  -v bsat-julia-depot:/opt/julia-depot \
  -w /workspace \
  bsat bash
The second -v keeps the Julia packages in a Docker volume named bsat-julia-depot instead of the container’s own disk, which --rm discards on exit. Docker creates the volume on first use. Use the same flag on every docker run so that every container finds the packages already installed.
Inside the container:
julia --project=code/model -e 'import Pkg; Pkg.instantiate(); Pkg.precompile()'   # first container only
cp code/model/path_license.txt.example code/model/path_license.txt                 # then edit the file
scripts/run_model_unix.sh
scripts/run_r_pipeline_unix.sh     # optional
View the results with the hosted dashboard at https://huggingface.co/spaces/bsat-team/BSAT_Viz (Dashboard) and upload the output package from output/. The repository folder is bind-mounted, so the package the container writes is already on the host; nothing has to be copied out of the container.
The run scripts find the container’s tools on their own: Julia on PATH, micromamba on PATH, the R environment at /opt/envs/bsat (or the folder named by BSAT_ENV) and the dashboard environment at /opt/envs/bsat-dashboard (or BSAT_DASHBOARD_ENV). A local install under .bsat_local/ or BSAT_LOCAL_DIR, if present, takes precedence.


Run a single script non-interactively
code/model/path_license.txt must exist on the host, since the repository folder is bind-mounted, and the Julia packages must already be in the bsat-julia-depot volume (run the Pkg.instantiate line above once):
docker run --rm -v "$(pwd):/workspace" -v bsat-julia-depot:/opt/julia-depot -w /workspace bsat bash scripts/run_model_unix.sh
After code/model/Manifest.toml changes (for example after pulling a new version of the repository), run the Pkg.instantiate line again to update the volume. To start from an empty depot, delete the volume with docker volume rm bsat-julia-depot.


Distributing the image without internet access
docker save bsat | gzip > bsat_image.tar.gz     # on the build machine
docker load < bsat_image.tar.gz                 # on the air-gapped host
Note that Pkg.instantiate() still needs access to the Julia package servers the first time it runs on each host, since the bsat-julia-depot volume is not part of the saved image; see Troubleshooting for proxies and mirrors.

title: Dashboard
text: The BSAT dashboard is a Streamlit application (code/visualization/) that reads one or two model output packages and compares the scenario solution with the baseline across regions, commodities, attributes and years.

title: Dashboard
text:
Hosted use
The dashboard is hosted on Hugging Face Spaces at https://huggingface.co/spaces/bsat-team/BSAT_Viz. Nothing needs to be installed; open the page, upload a package as “Shock 1” and optionally a second one as “Shock 2”. Uploaded files are held in memory for the session and are not stored.

title: Dashboard
text:
What the dashboard expects
A package is the Output.zip written by the model (Package and file format). The dashboard reads four of its seven files, at the archive root or inside a folder:








File
Role
Required




data_targets_adjusted.csv
baseline (the targets the model used)
yes


data_solution.csv
scenario solution
yes


data_shocks.csv
the shock inputs of the run
optional


METADATA.csv
field,value pairs describing the run
optional



data_params_calibrated.csv, data_exogenous.csv and SCENARIO_SOLVER_LOG.txt are ignored. Packages from older model versions that hold data_targets.csv instead of data_targets_adjusted.csv, possibly under an Output/ folder, are accepted as a fallback; a note says so when that file is used. The upload limit is 20 MB per package (set in code/visualization/.streamlit/config.toml and in bsat_dashboard.py, which the tests keep in agreement); a ten-year output package is about 1 MB.
For each package the dashboard drops the input-level baseline rows (attribute type RYNCI), translates the lowercase solution codes to the baseline display names (table), joins baseline and solution on region, commodity, year and attribute, and computes the ratio of solution to baseline and the percent change. A neutral run shows ratios of 1 everywhere. Duplicate keys, if any, keep the first row and produce a note.

title: Dashboard
text:
The views
Panels appear in this order; each opens from a header, and the charts come before the tables.

Metadata: the METADATA.csv of each package (author, description, model version, years requested and solved).
Time series: region, commodity, variable: the baseline path and each scenario path for one region, commodity and variable, labelled with the unit.
Regional changes: commodity, year, variable: percent change by region for a commodity, variable and year, side by side for two scenarios. Every region is labelled (names truncated to 20 characters; the tooltip has the full name).
Heatmap of changes: year, variable: percent change by region and commodity for a variable and year; with two scenarios a radio button picks the one shown. The color scale is symmetric around zero and spans the largest absolute change of either scenario in that view (at least 1 percent, at most 100 percent; larger changes take the end colors), so the same color means the same change in both heatmaps. Cells whose change rounds to 0.0 percent are white; region and commodity combinations without data are light gray.
Top Regional Changes: commodity, year, variable: the regions with the largest absolute percent change for a commodity, variable and year, for either scenario. Increases are red and decreases blue, the end colors of the heatmap scale, so small changes stay visible.
Table: Baseline Data: the baseline rows of either package, with column filters.
Table: Scenario Variables: the data_shocks.csv of each package, all rows or only the active shocks (value different from 0).

Regions, commodities and variables are shown by their display names (region_name, commodity_name, attribute_description of the uploaded files); the dropdowns list only what the data contain. The year lists start at the first solved year and open on the second one, the first year in which a shock can act, since the first year reproduces the observed data.

title: Dashboard
text:
Two-scenario comparison
With two packages, both scenarios are compared against the baseline of Shock 1: the second package’s solution is joined to the first package’s baseline. Every output package carries its own baseline, so this is exact whenever both runs used the same input targets, which is the normal case for scenarios derived from one baseline package with make_shock. If the two baselines differ (different keys, or values differing by more than a relative 1e-6), the dashboard shows the warning

The baseline in the Shock 2 package differs from the baseline in the Shock 1 package. Both scenarios are compared against the Shock 1 baseline.

and continues. Treat the comparison with care in that case: the percent changes of Shock 2 are then measured against a baseline its run did not use.

title: Dashboard
text:
Running locally
The hosted copy above is the recommended way to view results. It accepts any output package, wherever it was produced, and needs nothing installed. Running the dashboard server yourself only makes sense on an install on your own computer, where the server and the browser are on the same machine. In a codespace or a Docker container, download the output package to your own computer and use the hosted copy instead of the run script.

With the repository scripts
After the bootstrap (Local: macOS and Linux, Local: Windows):
scripts/run_dashboard_unix.sh
scripts\run_dashboard_windows.bat
The script starts streamlit run app.py from code/visualization/ in the bsat-dashboard conda environment (setup/environment-dashboard.yml: Python 3.11, pandas, numpy, altair, streamlit). Open http://localhost:8501.
This environment is separate from the bsat R environment of the pipeline and is optional: the bootstrap creates it last, treats a failure there as a warning, and skips it with --no-dashboard. Streamlit depends on pyarrow and libarrow, a large dependency tree that failed to extract on a locked-down Windows laptop; the hosted copy above needs nothing installed. If the environment is missing, the run script prints the hosted URL and exits; rerun the bootstrap without --no-dashboard to create it. The container image has the environment preinstalled at /opt/envs/bsat-dashboard.


With pip
From code/visualization/, with Python 3.10 or newer:
python -m venv venv
source venv/bin/activate        # Windows: venv\Scripts\activate
pip install "streamlit>=1.44.1" -r requirements.txt
streamlit run app.py
requirements.txt pins every package, direct and transitive (Streamlit 1.44.1, pandas 2.2.3, numpy 1.26.4, altair 5.5.0, pyarrow 19.0.1); the Space runs that Streamlit version on Python 3.10, as declared in the front matter of code/visualization/README.md. The app also runs on newer stacks (tested with Streamlit 1.63, pandas 3.0, altair 6.2).

title: Dashboard
text:
Code layout and tests

app.py: Streamlit entry point (layout, widgets, charts).
bsat_dashboard.py: the data functions (package parsing, merging, shock filtering, region labels, chart selections), with no Streamlit dependency. Documented in the Python reference.
tests/test_loaders.py: tests of the loaders on the committed example packages in data/outputs/ and on synthesized old-naming and mismatched-baseline packages. Run pytest tests/ from code/visualization/, or python tests/test_loaders.py when pytest is not installed.
.streamlit/config.toml: server settings (the upload size limit).

title: BSAT: Baseline Scenario Analysis Tool
text:
BSAT simulates how the USDA 10-year international agricultural baseline responds to policy and productivity shocks. It is a calibrated, multi-region partial-equilibrium model of 12 commodities (barley, beef, corn, cotton, pork, poultry, rice, sorghum, soybeans, soybean meal, soybean oil, wheat) in 42 countries and regions, solved year by year as a mixed complementarity problem with the PATH solver. With no shocks it reproduces the baseline projections exactly; with shocks it reports the new production, consumption, trade, stock and yield paths against that baseline.
The tool is built for analysts who want to ask “what if” questions of the baseline without writing model code. A scenario is a copy of the baseline input package in which one CSV file, data_shocks.csv, has been edited. Ten shock attributes are available per region, commodity and year: import tariffs, export taxes, non-tariff import and export measures, land productivity, total factor productivity in value added, in intermediate use and in livestock feed use, land supply, and the agricultural expenditure share. The edit can be made in a spreadsheet (a full or partial copy of the file, applied and run by one command), from the command line, or from Julia. The model turns the package into an output package, and a browser dashboard compares up to two output packages side by side.
