title: BSAT: Baseline Scenario Analysis Tool
text:
First run in five commands
From the repository root, after installing and adding the license:
scripts/run_model_unix.sh                                        # 1. baseline: output/baseline_Output.zip
julia --project=code/model code/model/make_shock.jl --list       # 2. the ten shock attributes
julia --project=code/model code/model/make_shock.jl \
      --template data/packages/baseline_2025_Input.zip \
      --inputpkg output/my_case_Input.zip \
      --shock shock_import_tariff --value 0.10 \
      --regions CHN --commodities Soybean --years 2026:2034 \
      --description "China soybean tariff +10 pp"                # 3. author a scenario
scripts/run_model_unix.sh output/my_case_Input.zip output/my_case_Output.zip   # 4. run it
# 5. open https://huggingface.co/spaces/bsat-team/BSAT_Viz and upload output/my_case_Output.zip
The output package carries the baseline it was solved against, so the dashboard shows the scenario against the baseline from that one file; a second package can be uploaded to compare two shocks. scripts/run_dashboard_unix.sh runs the dashboard server on your own computer and is not needed for this.
On Windows use scripts\run_model_windows.bat; the Julia commands are the same. The baseline run takes about two minutes and 1.6 GB of memory for the ten years 2025 to 2034.

title: Local installation: macOS and Linux
text:
Everything installs under .bsat_local/ inside the repository folder, or under the folder named by the BSAT_LOCAL_DIR environment variable if it is set. Nothing touches system directories, shell configuration files or package managers; PATH changes are made inside each script and discarded when it exits.
Disk space: about 4 to 6 GB. First run: 10 to 30 minutes, depending on network speed.

title: Local installation: macOS and Linux
text:
Prerequisites

macOS 12 or later, or a current Linux distribution (x86_64 or aarch64).
bash, curl and tar on your PATH (pre-installed on macOS and most Linux distributions).
No administrator or sudo rights.

title: Local installation: macOS and Linux
text:
Step 1: get the repository
git clone https://github.com/BSAT-team/BSAT.git
cd bsat
If you downloaded BSAT as a ZIP file instead (the green “Code” button on the repository page, then “Download ZIP”), unpack it, open your terminal application (macOS: Applications > Utilities > Terminal, or search “Terminal” in Spotlight; Linux: your usual terminal application) and cd into the unpacked folder. If the execute bit was stripped from the scripts:
chmod +x scripts/*.sh

title: Local installation: macOS and Linux
text:
Step 2: bootstrap
From the repository root:
scripts/bootstrap_unix.sh
The script:

Detects the platform (Linux x86_64, Linux aarch64, macOS Intel, macOS Apple Silicon).
Downloads micromamba 2.8.1 to .bsat_local/bin/.
Creates the bsat conda environment at .bsat_local/envs/bsat from setup/environment.yml (R 4.5 and the pipeline’s R packages). Required. An existing environment with another R version is recreated.
Downloads Julia 1.12.1 to .bsat_local/julia/.
Runs Pkg.instantiate() and Pkg.precompile() for code/model/Project.toml (JuMP, PATHSolver, CSV, DataFrames and the rest of the manifest).
Creates the bsat-dashboard conda environment at .bsat_local/envs/bsat-dashboard from setup/environment-dashboard.yml (Python 3.11, pandas, numpy, altair, streamlit). Optional: it is only needed to run the dashboard locally.

The two conda environments are separate on purpose. The model and the pipeline never needed Python; Streamlit pulls in pyarrow and libarrow, a large dependency tree that failed to extract on a locked-down Windows laptop. The bootstrap therefore creates the dashboard environment last, reports a failure there as a warning rather than an error, and finishes with “Bootstrap complete” either way. The hosted dashboard at https://huggingface.co/spaces/bsat-team/BSAT_Viz is the default way to view results, so the environment can be skipped:
scripts/bootstrap_unix.sh --no-dashboard
Each environment is created in a fresh folder (a partial environment from an interrupted run is removed first). If creation fails, the script clears the package cache (micromamba clean -a and .bsat_local/mamba/pkgs) and tries once more. An environment counts as already present when conda-meta/history exists in its folder.
To install somewhere other than .bsat_local/, set BSAT_LOCAL_DIR before the bootstrap and before every run script:
export BSAT_LOCAL_DIR=$HOME/bsat_local
scripts/bootstrap_unix.sh
Re-running the script is safe: completed steps are skipped. Do not move or rename the repository folder afterwards; the environment records absolute paths (see Troubleshooting).

title: Local installation: macOS and Linux
section: Step 3: add the PATH solver license
text:
Step 3: add the PATH solver license
The PATH solver needs a free license string at run time.

Open https://pages.cs.wisc.edu/~ferris/path/LICENSE and copy the string in the “Variable value” field.
Create the license file from the template:
cp code/model/path_license.txt.example code/model/path_license.txt
Edit code/model/path_license.txt and replace the placeholder line with the string. Lines starting with # and blank lines are ignored; the first other line is the license. Do not add quotes or extra spaces.

The runner reads this file at every start. It stops with a message if the file is missing, holds only comments, or still contains the placeholder.

title: Local installation: macOS and Linux
text:
Step 4: run the model
scripts/run_model_unix.sh
The script checks that Julia and the license file exist, creates the output folder, and runs code/model/run_model.jl on data/packages/baseline_2025_Input.zip for 2025 to 2034, writing output/baseline_Output.zip. It uses the portable Julia under .bsat_local/ when present and otherwise the julia on your PATH.
Arguments, all optional and positional:
scripts/run_model_unix.sh [Input.zip] [Output.zip] [years]
scripts/run_model_unix.sh output/my_case_Input.zip output/my_case_Output.zip 2025:2034
Progress and the PATH solver log print to the terminal and are also stored in SCENARIO_SOLVER_LOG.txt inside the output package. A ten-year run takes about two minutes.

title: Local installation: macOS and Linux
text:
Step 5: rebuild the inputs (optional)
scripts/run_r_pipeline_unix.sh
Runs Rscript main.R from code/processing/ inside the bsat environment. The pipeline rebuilds data/processed/*.csv and data/packages/baseline_2025_Input.zip from data/raw/. Two raw files are too large for the repository; see Raw data sources and scripts/fetch_large_raw_data.sh.

title: Local installation: macOS and Linux
text:
Step 6: run the dashboard locally (optional)
The dashboard is hosted online (Dashboard), which needs nothing installed. The hosted copy is the recommended way to view results and accepts output packages produced locally just as it does any other. The script below is only for running the dashboard server on your own computer; it needs the bsat-dashboard environment (bootstrap without --no-dashboard):
scripts/run_dashboard_unix.sh
This runs streamlit run app.py from code/visualization/ inside the bsat-dashboard environment (.bsat_local/envs/bsat-dashboard, then $BSAT_DASHBOARD_ENV, then /opt/envs/bsat-dashboard in the container). Open http://localhost:8501 and upload one or two output packages. If the environment is absent, the script says so and prints the hosted URL; rerun the bootstrap to create it.

text:
Notes

The scripts derive the repository path from their own location, so they can be run from any working directory.
All scripts honor BSAT_LOCAL_DIR; when it is unset they use .bsat_local/ inside the repository.
To reset the environment completely, delete .bsat_local/ (or the BSAT_LOCAL_DIR folder) and rerun scripts/bootstrap_unix.sh. This does not affect your code, data or path_license.txt.
To verify the installation end to end, run the model regression test (about four minutes): julia --project=code/model code/model/test/runtests.jl.

title: Troubleshooting
text: Entries are grouped by the step at which the problem appears. Paths are written with forward slashes; on Windows read code\model\path_license.txt for code/model/path_license.txt.

title: Troubleshooting
text:
PATH solver license
The runner reads code/model/path_license.txt at every start (or the file given with --license). Three messages are possible.
File missing. The run scripts stop before starting Julia:
Missing code/model/path_license.txt: paste your PATH license (see path_license.txt.example).
and the runner itself reports PATH license missing: create <path> with your license string. Fix: copy code/model/path_license.txt.example to code/model/path_license.txt and paste your string (installation guides, step 3).
Placeholder still in the file. The runner reports
code/model/path_license.txt still contains the placeholder line; paste your PATH license string.
Fix: open https://pages.cs.wisc.edu/~ferris/path/LICENSE, copy the “Variable value” string, and replace the line PASTE-YOUR-PATH-LICENSE-STRING-HERE.
Only comments in the file. The runner reports ... has no license string (only blanks and comments). Fix: add the license line.
Format: lines beginning with # and blank lines are ignored; the first other line is read as the license, without quotes or surrounding spaces.

title: Troubleshooting
section: The repository folder was moved or renamed
text:
The repository folder was moved or renamed
The portable environments under .bsat_local/envs/ record absolute paths. After moving or renaming the repository folder, the R and Python launchers point at the old location and fail. Fix: delete .bsat_local/envs/bsat (and .bsat_local/envs/bsat-dashboard if present) and rerun the bootstrap script (scripts/bootstrap_unix.sh or scripts\bootstrap_windows.bat); the other completed steps are skipped. An install placed elsewhere with BSAT_LOCAL_DIR is unaffected by moving the repository, but the same applies if that folder is moved.

title: Troubleshooting
text:
The model refuses a year
The console and SCENARIO_SOLVER_LOG.txt show, for one or more years,
All markets:   NOT CLEAR
...
Baseline Projections Data DO NOT clear in levels
No simulation is provided
Cause: in some market of that year, the supply-demand identity of the targets (beginning stocks plus production plus imports minus loss equals total consumption plus exports plus ending stocks) has a residual the model does not repair on its own, that is, one outside plus or minus 2. Within that window the model subtracts the residual from the largest of beginning stocks, production and imports (see Model). The runner skips the year, lists it under “Years skipped” in the log and in METADATA.csv, and continues with the next year; the output package holds the solved years only.
Fix: rebuild the targets with the pipeline, whose harmonization step (script 50) applies the model’s own three adjustments before the package is built, and inspect data/interim/harmonization_log.csv for the offending market-years: the status column flags every residual left outside the window. If you edited data_targets.csv by hand, restore the identity in that market.

title: Troubleshooting
section: The solver does not reach a solution
text:
The solver does not reach a solution
The log shows a termination status other than LOCALLY_SOLVED (or OPTIMAL) for a year, with the warning Simulation CANNOT be generated for baseline projections of the year .... The year is skipped and reported as above. Large shocks are the usual cause; try a smaller value or fewer simultaneous shocks and read the PATH iteration log in SCENARIO_SOLVER_LOG.txt.

title: Troubleshooting
section: The pipeline stops at the NTM step
text:
The pipeline stops at the NTM step
main.R stops with The NTM step needs BACI_HS92_Y2014_V202401b.csv, tariff_ave_2014_WITS.csv, ag_hs_products.csv under data/raw/trade_barriers/ ..., or the interim results NTM_IMP_ave_region.csv and NTM_EXP_ave_region.csv under data/interim/. Neither was found. A similar message for script 22 names tariff_ave_WITS_2023.csv and the interim results tariff_ave_region.csv and export_taxes_comm_reg.csv.
Scripts 22 and 23 need five raw files that are not distributed with the repository: BACI_HS92_Y2014_V202401b.csv and tariff_ave_2014_WITS.csv (too large), tariff_ave_WITS_2023.csv, ag_hs_products.csv and ag_tariff_USA_2014.xls (source terms). A clone from git ships the derived files in data/interim/ and skips both scripts, so this message means those derived files are missing (for example after deleting data/interim/): restore them with git checkout -- data/interim. To rerun the scripts from scratch instead, obtain the raw files (scripts/fetch_large_raw_data.sh reports which are present, downloads the CEPII file with --download, and prints how to obtain the WITS and WTO files). See Raw data sources.

title: Troubleshooting
text:
Runtime and memory
A ten-year run of the baseline package takes about two minutes and peaks at about 1.6 GB of memory on a workstation. PATH is single-threaded, so a laptop gives similar times; more cores do not help. If the machine swaps, close other applications or, in Docker, raise the container memory limit:
docker run --rm -it --memory=4g -v "$(pwd):/workspace" -v bsat-julia-depot:/opt/julia-depot -w /workspace bsat bash

Setting a proxy
Set the variables in the same shell or window before running any script.
set HTTP_PROXY=http://proxy.agency.gov:8080
set HTTPS_PROXY=http://proxy.agency.gov:8080
scripts\bootstrap_windows.bat
export HTTP_PROXY=http://proxy.agency.gov:8080
export HTTPS_PROXY=http://proxy.agency.gov:8080
scripts/bootstrap_unix.sh
curl (micromamba and Julia downloads) and micromamba honor these variables.


Julia package server
Julia’s package manager reads HTTP_PROXY and HTTPS_PROXY and also supports a dedicated variable. If your organization mirrors the Julia package server, point Julia at it before bootstrap or Pkg.instantiate():
export JULIA_PKG_SERVER=https://pkg.julialang.org

title: Troubleshooting
text:
micromamba cannot solve the environment
Symptom during bootstrap: critical libmamba Could not solve for environment specs or a similar conflict.

Network timeout during the solve: rerun the bootstrap script; completed steps are skipped and the solve is retried.
Stale package cache: delete .bsat_local/mamba/pkgs/ and rerun.
Partial environment on disk: delete .bsat_local/envs/bsat and rerun (the bootstrap does this itself when conda-meta/history is missing from the folder).

title: Troubleshooting
text:
Package cache errors during extraction
Symptom during bootstrap, typically while the optional bsat-dashboard environment is being created on Windows:
error libmamba Invalid package cache
error libmamba Cannot find a valid extracted directory cache for <package>
The package named has been azure-storage-files-datalake-cpp, a libarrow dependency of Streamlit and so of the dashboard environment. The bsat R environment has no such dependency. Causes seen so far:

Long paths: some of these packages unpack into folders whose full path exceeds the 260-character Windows limit, and extraction fails silently until libmamba finds the cache incomplete.
A download interrupted by a corporate proxy, leaving a truncated archive in the cache.
Antivirus software quarantining files while they are being extracted.

Fixes, in order:

Rerun the bootstrap. Its environment step removes the partial environment, clears the package cache (micromamba clean -a and .bsat_local/mamba/pkgs) and retries once.
Install to a short path: set BSAT_LOCAL_DIR=C:\bsat_local (Windows) or export BSAT_LOCAL_DIR=$HOME/bsat_local, then rerun the bootstrap. The run scripts read the same variable.
Skip the dashboard environment with scripts\bootstrap_windows.bat --no-dashboard (or scripts/bootstrap_unix.sh --no-dashboard) and use the hosted dashboard at https://huggingface.co/spaces/bsat-team/BSAT_Viz. The model and the pipeline do not use this environment; a failure there is reported as a warning and the bootstrap still completes.
Ask IT to enable long paths (a registry setting that needs administrator rights) or to add the install folder to the antivirus allowlist.

title: Troubleshooting
text:
Julia package instantiation fails
Symptom: bootstrap fails at Pkg.instantiate(), or the model stops with a LoadError for a missing package.
Reset the portable Julia and its depot, then rerun bootstrap, which reinstalls every package pinned in code/model/Manifest.toml:
rm -rf .bsat_local/julia
scripts/bootstrap_unix.sh
rmdir /s /q .bsat_local\julia
scripts\bootstrap_windows.bat
PATHSolver downloads the native PATH library as an artifact during instantiation. If that download is blocked, confirm the artifact host is allowed, set JULIA_PKG_SERVER to a mirror, or use the container option (Cloud and Docker).

title: Troubleshooting
section: The run script cannot find Julia or micromamba
text:
The run script cannot find Julia or micromamba
Julia not found. Run scripts/bootstrap_unix.sh first (local install), or use the devcontainer. or micromamba not found ...: the Unix scripts look under the install folder first and then on PATH; the Windows scripts look under the install folder only. The install folder is .bsat_local/ inside the repository, or BSAT_LOCAL_DIR when that variable is set: if you bootstrapped with BSAT_LOCAL_DIR set, set it again in every new window. Run the bootstrap script, or (Unix) put julia and micromamba on PATH. The R environment is resolved as <install folder>/envs/bsat, then $BSAT_ENV, then /opt/envs/bsat (the container); the dashboard environment as <install folder>/envs/bsat-dashboard, then $BSAT_DASHBOARD_ENV, then /opt/envs/bsat-dashboard.

title: Troubleshooting
section: The dashboard script reports a missing environment
text:
The dashboard script reports a missing environment
bsat-dashboard environment not found ... followed by the hosted URL: the optional Python environment was skipped (--no-dashboard) or failed to build (a warning near the end of the bootstrap output). Use the hosted dashboard, or rerun the bootstrap without --no-dashboard; see Package cache errors during extraction if it fails again.

title: Troubleshooting
section: Running the R pipeline from another directory
text:
Running the R pipeline from another directory
main.R sets its own working directory to code/processing/ whether it is run through Rscript, source() or RStudio, so relative paths inside the scripts resolve. The data root defaults to <repo>/data; to use data elsewhere set BSAT_DATA_DIR to a folder containing raw/ (interim/ and processed/ are created there). Running a single numbered script on its own requires source("R/00_load_packages.R") first and code/processing/ as the working directory, or options(bsat.data_dir = "...").

title: Troubleshooting
text:
General reset
Removes all downloaded software and both environments; does not touch code, data or path_license.txt. Replace .bsat_local with the BSAT_LOCAL_DIR folder if you set one:
rm -rf .bsat_local
scripts/bootstrap_unix.sh
rmdir /s /q .bsat_local
scripts\bootstrap_windows.bat

title: Data processing pipeline
text: code/processing/ holds the R pipeline that turns the public raw files in data/raw/ into the four model input CSVs in data/processed/ and the input package in data/packages/. main.R sources the numbered scripts in code/processing/R/ in order; every script starts with rm(list = ls()), reads its inputs from files and writes its outputs to files, so the scripts communicate only through data/interim/ and data/processed/. The header block at the top of each script (Purpose, Reads, Writes, Depends, Notes) is the authoritative description; this page collects those headers. Sources and download links for every raw file are in Raw data sources; the refresh procedure for a new data vintage is in Updating raw data.

title: Data processing pipeline
text:
How to run
Three equivalent entry points:

scripts/run_r_pipeline_unix.sh (Linux, macOS, WSL): runs Rscript main.R from code/processing/ inside the bsat micromamba environment created by scripts/bootstrap_unix.sh (or the devcontainer environment).
scripts\run_r_pipeline_windows.bat: the same, using the portable environment under .bsat_local\ created by scripts\bootstrap_windows.bat.
Rscript main.R from code/processing/, with R 4.4 or later that has the packages listed in R/00_load_packages.R (nothing is installed; a missing package stops the run with its name). main.R also runs from RStudio (source("main.R")); it sets the working directory to its own folder either way.

Data location. main.R resolves the data root as <repo>/data and stores it in the R option bsat.data_dir; every script reads it with base_dir <- getOption("bsat.data_dir", file.path("..", "..", "data")). To use data kept elsewhere, set the environment variable BSAT_DATA_DIR to a folder that contains raw/; main.R creates interim/ and processed/ under it:
BSAT_DATA_DIR=/path/to/data scripts/run_r_pipeline_unix.sh
A single script can be run on its own after source("R/00_load_packages.R"), with code/processing/ as the working directory (the fallback ../../data then points at the repository data folder) or after options(bsat.data_dir = "...").
Order of execution in main.R: 00 01 10 11 12 20 21 [22] [23] 24 30 40 50 60. Script 50 runs last, right before packaging, so that script 20 computes the expenditure share from the unrepaired quantities of script 12, as the model authors do. Scripts 22 and 23 run only when their raw inputs that are not distributed with the repository are present; otherwise main.R reuses the derived files shipped in data/interim/ (see “Large files and the NTM step”). Script 25 is never sourced (see “Diagnostics”). A full run takes a few minutes; script 23, when it runs, adds several more because it reads the 460 MB BACI file.

title: Data processing pipeline
text:
What the pipeline produces
data/processed/ (tracked in git) holds the four model inputs, all in the same long schema (region, year, nest, commodity, input, attribute, value, unit, attribute_type, attribute_description, region_name, nest_name, commodity_name):

data_targets.csv: baseline levels the model is calibrated to (area, yield, production, imports, exports, consumption, stocks, feed use by livestock product) for 42 regions, 12 commodities and the crop years 2025 to 2034.
data_exogenous.csv: levels of the exogenous drivers: calibrated elasticities and productivity parameters, international prices, population and GDP per capita, import tariffs and export taxes, non-tariff measures, land cost shares (phi_f), livestock inventory and slaughter, and unit price normalizations.
data_shocks.csv: a zero-filled scaffold of the ten shock attributes for every region, commodity and year. Editing it defines a counterfactual scenario.
data_params_init.csv: initial values of the seven commodity-level elasticities.

data/packages/baseline_2025_Input.zip (tracked) bundles the four CSVs plus a METADATA.csv in the Input/ layout the model runner reads (Package and file format). Because the shocks are neutral, running the model on it reproduces the USDA baseline.
data/interim/ (regenerated by every run; untracked except the five derived files that replace raw inputs not distributed with the repository, see “Large files and the NTM step”) holds the intermediate files listed under each script below, including harmonization_log.csv, which records every market-year with a nonzero consumption or supply-demand residual and what script 50 did with it.

title: Data processing pipeline
text:
Scripts

00_load_packages.R

Purpose: check that every package the pipeline uses is installed and attach it; nothing is installed. Sourced first by main.R; later scripts clear objects but keep the attached packages. A missing or broken package stops the run with its name.
Reads: none.
Writes: none.
Depends: dplyr, tidyr, stringr, readr, readxl, openxlsx, zip, data.table, lfe, ggplot2 (from setup/environment.yml)
Notes: stringr, data.table and ggplot2 are loaded but no numbered script currently calls them; lfe is used only by 23.



01_check_region_commodity_coverage.R

Purpose: expand the region-commodity list of the USDA baseline to the full region x commodity grid and flag the pairs the baseline does not cover.
Reads: raw/region_commodity_list_2025.xlsx (sheet Sheet1, columns region, commodity).
Writes: interim/region_commodity_coverage.csv.
Notes: audit only; no later script reads the output.



10_read_baseline_data.R

Purpose: read the commodity sheets of the USDA International Long-Term Projections workbook and reshape them into one long table (commodity x region x year) holding the baseline variables.
Reads: raw/2025 International Long-Term Projections to 2034.xlsx (one sheet per commodity); raw/region_commodity_list_2025.xlsx (region order within each sheet).
Writes: interim/baseline_projections_long.csv.
Notes: the workbook name is the constant baseline_data. The sheet layout is hard-coded: region blocks are 25 rows apart and 21 rows tall, starting at row 9 (Poultry) or row 7 (other commodities); the number and meaning of the columns per commodity group is fixed in the script; the regions of a sheet are those of the region list, in order, followed by World. The string -- marks missing values; crop years such as 2025/26 keep the first year.



11_compute_feed_use_decomposition.R

Purpose: split each region’s total feed use of every feed crop across beef, pork and poultry in proportion to FAOSTAT livestock value-of-production shares.
Reads: raw/mapping.csv; raw/FAOSTAT_total_livestock_value_constant_IntlD.csv; raw/FAOSTAT_each_livestock_value_constant_IntlD.csv; interim/baseline_projections_long.csv.
Writes: interim/livestock_value_shares.xlsx; interim/feed_use_decomposition.xlsx.
Notes: feed use of a crop is feed_only + ind_feed_other + feed_seed_waste for Barley, Corn, Sorghum, Soybeans, Soybean meal, Soybean oil and Wheat, and is split by the 2015 value shares. A missing value share is read as no demand. Myanmar is recoded MMR to BUR. Only group A regions and years from 2025 are kept.



12_generate_data_targets.R

Purpose: build data_targets.csv from the long baseline table and the feed-use decomposition.
Reads: interim/baseline_projections_long.csv; interim/feed_use_decomposition.xlsx; raw/mapping.csv; raw/baseline_units.csv.
Writes: processed/data_targets.csv (overwritten afterwards by script 50).
Notes: lst_obsv_yr <- 2025 is the first year of the analysis period and must equal first_yr in script 30. Commodities are renamed to model codes (Beef, SoyMeal, SoyOil, Soybean) and assigned to nests. A soybean-market consistency check reallocates SoyOil in BGD to OAO and SoyOil and SoyMeal in ECO to ONA when those regions have soy product projections but no soybean market. Quantity attributes are rounded to whole units; yields and extraction rates are not (script 50 re-derives them).



20_compute_ag_expenditure_share.R

Purpose: compute the agricultural expenditure share (spending on the twelve modeled commodities as a percentage of real GDP) by region for 2025, and save the annual international price series built along the way.
Reads: processed/data_targets.csv; raw/2026-06-19 IMF Commodity Prices external-data.xlsx (sheet External); raw/2026-06-19 International Prices FAO Meat.xlsx (sheet data); raw/2026-06-24 CPI_US.xlsx (sheet Sheet1); raw/Global GDP Shares and GDP Growth Assumptions to 2035.xlsx; raw/mapping.csv.
Writes: interim/international_prices_annual.csv (marketing-year averages, native units, all years); interim/ag_expenditure_shares.csv.
Notes: IMF series are picked by the code in row 1 (PBARL, PWHEAMT, PCOTTIND, PRICENPQ, PMAIZMT, PSORG, PSOYB, PSMEA, PSOIL); FAO meat prices are simple averages of fixed column positions. Prices are deflated to 2017 USD with CPI_2017 and averaged over USDA marketing years; an incomplete last year uses the last 12 observed months. The GDP workbook is read by column position and its region labels must match the crosswalk in the script. Only 2025 is exported.



21_compute_land_cost_share.R

Purpose: compute the land cost share of value added (phi_f) for every region and crop from U.S. per-acre variable costs, relative yields and the USDA international TFP land cost shares.
Reads: raw/AgTFPInternational2023.xlsx (sheet Cost Shares); the five workbooks in raw/variable_costs_2025/ matching vc_pattern <- "to 2035"; raw/mapping.csv; interim/baseline_projections_long.csv.
Writes: interim/variable_costs_us_2025.csv; interim/region_commodity_land_cost_shares.csv.
Notes: the EUR land share is hard-coded at 0.113. Cost workbooks are parsed by row label (Table ... U.S. <crop>, Item, Variable costs of production, Per acre). Land rents solve a one-equation root-finding problem per region and year; shares are winsorized at the 5th and 95th percentiles within each year. Years from 2025 are exported.



22_compute_tariff_ave.R

Purpose: compute region-commodity ad valorem import tariffs (simple average of WITS MFN tariffs, latest reported year per product) and a zero export-tax scaffold.
Reads: raw/trade_barriers/tariff_ave_WITS_2023.csv (not distributed); raw/trade_barriers/country_code_WITS.xlsx; raw/mapping.csv.
Writes: interim/tariff_ave_region.csv; interim/export_taxes_comm_reg.csv (both tracked in git as the shipped derived products).
Notes: sourced by main.R only when the WITS 2023 extract is present; otherwise the two shipped outputs are reused. HS codes are mapped to commodities by fixed 4- and 6-digit lists. Missing tariffs are set to 0 (with the current data: all of Iraq, Saudi Arabia pork, Pakistan soybean oil). The EU is one reporter (EUN). Export taxes are not observed and are 0 everywhere. The year column of the tariff output is the string 2023 (or last observed).



23_compute_NTM_ave.R

Purpose: estimate a model of non-tariff-measure ad valorem equivalents (AVE) on tariffs, GDP per capita and agricultural imports with region x product fixed effects, impute missing AVEs, and aggregate them into GDP-weighted region-commodity import NTMs; export NTMs are a zero scaffold.
Reads: under raw/trade_barriers/: ave_hs_importer.csv, BACI_HS92_Y2014_V202401b.csv (not distributed), country_codes_V202401b.csv, ag_hs_products.csv (not distributed), ag_tariff_USA_2014.xls (not distributed, optional), tariff_ave_2014_WITS.csv (not distributed), country_code_WITS.xlsx, country_region_WB.xlsx; under raw/: current_GDPpc_2014_WB.csv, current_GDP_2014_WB.csv, current_GDPpc_IMF.xls, current_GDP_IMF.xls, mapping.csv; interim/commodity_hs6_mapping.csv when the WTO schedule is absent.
Writes: interim/model_estimates.RData; interim/NTM_regression_results.csv and interim/NTM_regression_table.tex (regression coefficients, standard errors and fit statistics, as CSV and as a LaTeX table for the paper); interim/NTM_ave_imputed.RData; interim/NTM_IMP_ave_region.csv; interim/NTM_EXP_ave_region.csv; interim/commodity_hs6_mapping.csv (rewritten only when the WTO schedule is present).
Notes: sourced by main.R only when BACI_HS92_Y2014_V202401b.csv, tariff_ave_2014_WITS.csv and ag_hs_products.csv are all present; otherwise the two shipped NTM outputs are reused. The commodity-to-HS6 mapping is rebuilt from ag_tariff_USA_2014.xls when that file is present and read from the shipped interim/commodity_hs6_mapping.csv otherwise. Regression: ave ~ AVE_Tariff + AVE_Tariff_ag + log_GDPpc + log_total_imp_ag | region_geo:product_id (felm). Negative imputations are set to 0; gaps for Barley, Sorghum, Soybeans and Wheat take the country’s Corn, Rice and Cotton average; Iraq takes its geographic-region average. All inputs refer to 2014.



24_generate_data_exogenous.R

Purpose: assemble data_exogenous.csv from the calibrated parameters, 2025 international prices, population and GDP per capita, unit price normalizations, livestock inventory and slaughter, and the interim results of scripts 20 to 23.
Reads: raw/exogenous_data.csv; raw/mapping.csv; raw/population_WB_2025.xls; raw/population_IMF_WEO_2025.csv; raw/Current_GDP_WB_2025.xls; raw/Current_GDP_IMF_WEO_2025.csv; raw/FAOSTAT_Livestock_Inventory_2024.csv; raw/FAOSTAT_Slaughtered Livestock_2024.csv; interim/international_prices_annual.csv; interim/ag_expenditure_shares.csv; interim/region_commodity_land_cost_shares.csv; interim/tariff_ave_region.csv; interim/export_taxes_comm_reg.csv; interim/NTM_IMP_ave_region.csv; interim/NTM_EXP_ave_region.csv.
Writes: processed/data_exogenous.csv.
Notes: prices, population and GDP use 2025; livestock inventory and slaughter use FAOSTAT year 2024. The IMF WEO files supply Taiwan only. Prices become million 2017 USD per 1,000 native units (cotton: 1,000 480-lb bales). baseline_units.csv is declared as an input but not read.



30_generate_data_shocks.R

Purpose: generate data_shocks.csv, a zero-filled scaffold of every shock attribute for each region, commodity and year of the analysis period.
Reads: raw/mapping.csv.
Writes: processed/data_shocks.csv.
Notes: first_yr <- 2025 and last_yr <- 2034 define the horizon; keep first_yr equal to lst_obsv_yr in script 12. Ten shock attributes: four trade barriers (all commodities), TFP value added and land productivity (crops), TFP feed use (livestock), TFP intermediates (SoyMeal, SoyOil), and two region-level shocks (ag expenditure share, land supply). Two attribute names contain spaces.



40_generate_data_params_init.R

Purpose: generate data_params_init.csv, the initial values of the seven commodity-level substitution and transformation elasticities.
Reads: none.
Writes: processed/data_params_init.csv.
Notes: values are hard-coded in the script: sigma_d 3.8, sigma_f 1.1, sigma_c 5, sigma_l 0.25, sigma_z 0.5, sigma_w 3.8, omega_s 5; 42 rows.



50_harmonize_targets.R

Purpose: apply to the rounded targets of script 12 the same three adjustments the model would make on its own, in the model’s order, so that the model finds no residual to repair.
Reads: processed/data_targets.csv.
Writes: processed/data_targets.csv (overwritten); interim/harmonization_log.csv (columns region, year, commodity, check, residual, adjusted, delta, status).
Notes: the three adjustments, in order. (a) A consumption residual (total consumption less food consumption, feed to livestock, other feed and crushing) within plus or minus 2 is added to the largest of those components, the first maximum in that order; when the largest is feed to livestock or other feed, the rows are left alone and the residual is left to the model (status left to the model: feed component): the model repairs it in its internal feed totals but reports feed consumption from the unrepaired target, so an untouched row is what reproduces its output. (b) A supply-demand residual within plus or minus 2 is subtracted from the largest of beginning stocks, production and imports, the first maximum in that order. (c) Yields are derived as production over area (cotton via 217.728111162486 kg per bale) and extraction rates as 100 times production over soybean crushing, both from the adjusted values. A residual outside plus or minus 2 is left alone, logged with a status containing outside the model's ±2 window and warned about; the model then refuses that year. With these adjustments the model’s run on the package gives the same solution as its run on the unharmonized targets (the regression test checks this against the model authors’ own package), and the neutral run reproduces every target exactly. Inspect the log after every run.



60_build_input_package.R

Purpose: bundle the four processed CSV files and a METADATA.csv into the standard model input package (a zip with an Input/ folder) specified in Package and file format.
Reads: the four files in processed/.
Writes: packages/baseline_<first year>_Input.zip, where the first year is the smallest year in data_targets.csv (currently baseline_2025_Input.zip).
Notes: METADATA.csv records author, description, comments and the build timestamp. An existing zip with the same name is replaced.

title: Data processing pipeline
section: Large files and the NTM step
text:
Large files and the NTM step
Five inputs of scripts 22 and 23 are not distributed with the repository (they are listed in .gitignore), all under data/raw/trade_barriers/:

BACI_HS92_Y2014_V202401b.csv (CEPII BACI, HS92, release 202401b, 2014 file; about 460 MB, too large for git).
tariff_ave_2014_WITS.csv (World Bank WITS, 2014 applied tariff ad valorem equivalents; about 245 MB, too large for git).
tariff_ave_WITS_2023.csv (WITS, MFN applied tariffs, 2023 or last observed; UNCTAD TRAINS terms).
ag_hs_products.csv (WITS product group WTO_HS_Aggri; UNCTAD TRAINS terms).
ag_tariff_USA_2014.xls (WTO Tariff and Trade Data, United States applied MFN schedule 2014; WTO terms).

In their place the repository tracks the derived products in data/interim/: tariff_ave_region.csv and export_taxes_comm_reg.csv (outputs of script 22), commodity_hs6_mapping.csv (the commodity-to-HS6 mapping that script 23 derives from the WTO schedule, 67 HS6 codes), and NTM_IMP_ave_region.csv and NTM_EXP_ave_region.csv (outputs of script 23, shipped the same way). The rest of data/interim/ stays untracked.
scripts/fetch_large_raw_data.sh (and scripts\fetch_large_raw_data.bat) reports which of the five files is present. With --download it fetches the BACI archive from CEPII (about 2.4 GB, resumable) and extracts only the 2014 file. The WITS and WTO files cannot be downloaded by a script: it prints how to obtain them (WITS Advanced Query, TRAINS, all reporters, all partners, all HS6 products, year 2014 or 2023, AVE of applied tariff, CSV export; the WTO_HS_Aggri product group as CSV; the WTO export of the United States applied MFN schedule for 2014) and the names to save them under. Terms of use and the exact query settings are in Raw data sources.
main.R decides at run time what to do with scripts 22 and 23:

Script 22 is sourced when tariff_ave_WITS_2023.csv exists; it regenerates interim/tariff_ave_region.csv and interim/export_taxes_comm_reg.csv. Otherwise, if both derived files exist, main.R prints 22_compute_tariff_ave: SKIPPED (WITS 2023 extract absent) and script 24 reads them as they are. If neither is available, main.R stops with a message naming the missing file.
Script 23 is sourced when BACI_HS92_Y2014_V202401b.csv, tariff_ave_2014_WITS.csv and ag_hs_products.csv all exist; it regenerates interim/NTM_IMP_ave_region.csv, interim/NTM_EXP_ave_region.csv, interim/model_estimates.RData and interim/NTM_ave_imputed.RData. Otherwise, if interim/NTM_IMP_ave_region.csv and interim/NTM_EXP_ave_region.csv both exist, main.R prints 23_compute_NTM_ave: SKIPPED (large raw files absent) and script 24 reads them as they are. If neither is available, main.R stops with a message naming the missing files, and scripts 24, 30, 40 and 50 do not run.
Inside script 23, the WTO schedule ag_tariff_USA_2014.xls is optional: when present, the commodity-to-HS6 mapping is rebuilt from it and interim/commodity_hs6_mapping.csv is rewritten; when absent, the shipped mapping is read and a message says so. The script stops only if both are missing.

A fresh clone therefore runs end to end from the tracked files alone, skipping scripts 22 and 23. The five raw files are needed only to rebuild the derived products, for instance after a change to the tariff mapping or the NTM imputation.

title: Data processing pipeline
text:
Diagnostics
R/25_compare_actual_imputed_NTM.R checks the quality of the NTM imputation in script 23. It is not sourced by main.R. It reads interim/NTM_ave_imputed.RData and writes to data/outputs/diagnostics/ (created if needed):

actual_vs_imputed_AVE.pdf: scatter plot of actual against imputed AVE for the country-commodity pairs that have both, with a fitted line, its slope and the number of observations.
NTM_AVE_diagnostics.xlsx: one sheet of metadata and four sheets listing the pairs whose AVE could not be imputed, those with no actual AVE, those where a missing actual AVE received a positive imputation, and those where the imputation failed (missing or negative).

Run it manually after script 23 has run (it therefore needs the raw files of script 23 that are not distributed), from code/processing/:
Rscript -e 'source("R/00_load_packages.R"); source("R/25_compare_actual_imputed_NTM.R")'
Set options(bsat.data_dir = "...") before the second source() if the data live outside <repo>/data.

title: Python reference: bsat_dashboard
text:
code/visualization/bsat_dashboard.py holds the data functions of the dashboard. Everything in it is independent of Streamlit so that it can be imported and tested without the Streamlit runtime; app.py wraps the loaders with st.cache_data and renders the results. Paths below are relative to code/visualization/.
A model output package is a ZIP archive written by the BSAT model. The current naming places data_targets_adjusted.csv (baseline), data_solution.csv (scenario solution), data_shocks.csv (shock inputs) and METADATA.csv (field,value pairs) at the archive root. Older packages store data_targets.csv instead of data_targets_adjusted.csv and may nest the files under a folder such as Output/. Both layouts are accepted; the older name produces a note that is surfaced to the user.

data_solution.csv, data_shocks.csv, METADATA.csv
Member names


MERGE_KEYS
["region", "commodity", "year", "attribute"]
Columns that identify one observation in both baseline and solution files


SOLUTION_ATTRIBUTE_NAMES
dict
Lowercase attribute codes of data_solution.csv mapped to the display names of the baseline; unlisted codes are kept unchanged (table)


SHOCK_TOLERANCE
1e-12
A shock is active whenever its value is farther than this from zero


BASELINE_RTOL
1e-6
Relative tolerance used when deciding whether two baselines agree


RATIO_DECIMALS
4
Decimals kept for ratios; percent changes are rounded to 2


NAME_COLUMNS
dict
Code column to display-name column: region to region_name, commodity to commodity_name, attribute to attribute_description

title: Python reference: bsat_dashboard
text:
ScenarioPackage
@dataclass
class ScenarioPackage:
    baseline: pd.DataFrame
    solution: pd.DataFrame
    notes: list[str]
Contents of one model output package relevant to the dashboard. baseline: tidy baseline rows with columns region, commodity, year, attribute, value, unit, region_name (unit and region_name may be missing when the source file lacks them). solution: solution rows with MERGE_KEYS plus value_scenario. notes: human-readable notes about fallbacks or data repairs performed while loading, for display in the app.

title: Python reference: bsat_dashboard
text:
ZIP helpers

find_member
find_member(names: list[str], filename: str) -> str | None
Find an archive member by base name, at the root or under any folder. names are the member names from ZipFile.namelist(); filename is the base name (case sensitive). Returns the full member name, preferring the shallowest match, or None.


read_csv_member
read_csv_member(zip_source, filename: str) -> pd.DataFrame | None
Read one CSV member of a package into a DataFrame. zip_source is a path to the ZIP or an open binary file object (rewound before reading). Returns the parsed table, or None when the member is absent.


load_metadata
load_metadata(zip_source) -> pd.DataFrame | None
Load METADATA.csv (columns field and value) from a package.


load_shocks
load_shocks(zip_source) -> pd.DataFrame | None
Load data_shocks.csv from a package.

title: Python reference: bsat_dashboard
text:
Shock table

changed_shocks
changed_shocks(shocks: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame
Keep only shock rows whose value differs from the neutral value zero. All shock attributes written by the model are decimals added to the baseline level (0.10 means +10 percentage points or +10 percent), so a value of zero leaves the baseline unchanged. Returns the subset of rows that represent an active shock.

title: Python reference: bsat_dashboard
text:
Baseline and solution

find_baseline_member
find_baseline_member(names: list[str]) -> tuple[str | None, str | None]
Locate the baseline file using the current name first, then fallbacks. Returns (member_name, note) where note is None for the current file name and a message for a fallback; (None, None) when absent.


tidy_baseline
tidy_baseline(df: pd.DataFrame, notes: list[str]) -> pd.DataFrame
Reduce a baseline file to the columns and rows used by the dashboard. Input-level rows (non-empty input column, attribute type RYNCI) describe feed inputs to a commodity and have no counterpart in the solution, so they are dropped before checking uniqueness. notes receives notes about repairs performed (duplicated keys keep the first row). Returns the tidy baseline with MERGE_KEYS plus value and, when present, unit and region_name.


tidy_solution
tidy_solution(df: pd.DataFrame, notes: list[str]) -> pd.DataFrame
Reduce a solution file to merge keys and the scenario value. Attribute codes are translated to the baseline’s display names through SOLUTION_ATTRIBUTE_NAMES. Returns a table with MERGE_KEYS plus value_scenario. Raises ValueError if the solution file has no value column.


load_scenario_package
load_scenario_package(zip_source) -> ScenarioPackage
Load baseline and solution tables from one model output package. Returns a ScenarioPackage with tidy baseline, tidy solution and notes. Raises ValueError if the baseline or solution file cannot be found.


baselines_agree
baselines_agree(first: pd.DataFrame, second: pd.DataFrame) -> bool
Check whether two tidy baselines have the same keys and values. Returns True when both tables cover the same keys with values equal up to BASELINE_RTOL.


merge_scenarios
merge_scenarios(package_1: ScenarioPackage, package_2: ScenarioPackage | None = None) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, list[str]]
Join the baseline with one or two scenario solutions. Each scenario contributes a ratio solution / baseline and the implied shocked value. The baseline of scenario 1 is the reference for both scenarios; a warning note is produced if scenario 2 ships a different one. Returns (df, notes) where df has the baseline columns plus ratio, pct_change and value_with_shock1 and, with a second package, ratio_shock2 and value_with_shock2.

title: Python reference: bsat_dashboard
section: Lookups derived from the merged table
text:
Lookups derived from the merged table

display_names
display_names(df: pd.DataFrame, code_column: str, name_column: str) -> dict[str, str]
Map the codes present in df to display names, {code: name} for every code in the data, using the first name found for each code and the code itself when no name is available.


label_maps
label_maps(df: pd.DataFrame) -> dict[str, dict[str, str]]
Display-name maps for regions, commodities and attributes, {"region": {...}, "commodity": {...}, "attribute": {...}}, built with display_names from the NAME_COLUMNS (region_name, commodity_name, attribute_description). The dropdowns of every view use these maps.


first_scenario_year
first_scenario_year(df: pd.DataFrame) -> int
Return the first year for which the scenario solution has values: the smallest year with a non-missing ratio; falls back to the smallest year in the table when no ratio is available.


scenario_years
scenario_years(df: pd.DataFrame) -> list[int]
List the years at or after first_scenario_year present in df.

Chart data

top_n_changes
top_n_changes(df, commodity: str, attribute: str, year: int, shock: str = "shock1", top_n: int = 10) -> pd.DataFrame
Select the regions with the largest absolute percent change for a commodity, attribute and year. shock is "shock1" or "shock2" (falls back to shock 1 if the second scenario is absent). Rows of one region, commodity and attribute, sorted by year.

Rows of one attribute and year, optionally restricted to a commodity.

title: Updating raw data
text:
This page describes what to do when a source publishes a new data vintage. The general procedure is the same for every file:
Files are grouped by source. “Consumed by” names the scripts in code/processing/R/. Year constants that must move together with the vintage are collected in “Moving the analysis period”.

title: Updating raw data
text:
USDA baseline

2025 International Long-Term Projections to 2034.xlsx

Consumed by: 10_read_baseline_data.R.
Constant: baseline_data <- "2025 International Long-Term Projections to 2034.xlsx".
To update: drop the new workbook in data/raw/, edit baseline_data, update region_commodity_list_2025.xlsx if the set of regions per commodity changed, rerun.
Assumptions: one sheet per commodity named exactly Barley, Beef and veal, Corn, Cotton, Pork, Poultry, Rice, Sorghum, Soybeans, Soybean meal, Soybean oil, Wheat. Within a sheet, region tables appear in the order of the region list followed by World, each 25 rows apart; the first data block spans rows 9 to 29 for Poultry and rows 7 to 27 for every other commodity, and holds 6 (Poultry, Beef and veal, Pork), 8 (Rice), 9 (Cotton), 10 (Barley, Corn, Sorghum, Wheat, Soybean meal, Soybean oil) or 11 (Soybeans) columns whose meaning is fixed in the script. Missing values are the string --; the year column holds crop years such as 2025/26. Any change in the row spacing, the starting row, the column set of a commodity group, or the region order breaks the read silently (values land under the wrong name), so compare data/interim/baseline_projections_long.csv against the workbook for a few regions after the first run.



region_commodity_list_2025.xlsx

Consumed by: 01_check_region_commodity_coverage.R, 10_read_baseline_data.R.
Constant: input_path_list <- file.path(base_dir, "raw", "region_commodity_list_2025.xlsx") in both scripts.
To update: project-maintained. Rebuild it from the new workbook’s table of contents (one row per region and commodity, in the order the regions appear in each commodity sheet), edit the two constants, rerun.
Assumptions: sheet Sheet1 with columns region and commodity; region names must match those in mapping.csv (column region) and commodity names must match the sheet names of the baseline workbook.



baseline_units.csv

Consumed by: 12_generate_data_targets.R (declared but not read by 24_generate_data_exogenous.R).
Constant: input_path_units <- file.path(base_dir, "raw", "baseline_units.csv").
To update: project-maintained; edit in place only if the baseline changes units (for example cotton bales).
Assumptions: columns commodity, commodity_name, attribute_description, unit, joined on commodity (model code) and attribute_description.

title: Updating raw data
text:
Macro and population

Current_GDP_WB_2025.xls and population_WB_2025.xls

Consumed by: 24_generate_data_exogenous.R.
Constants: input_path_GDP_WB <- file.path(base_dir, "raw", "Current_GDP_WB_2025.xls") and input_path_population_WB <- file.path(base_dir, "raw", "population_WB_2025.xls").
To update: download the World Bank indicator files (NY.GDP.MKTP.CD, SP.POP.TOTL) in Excel format, drop them in data/raw/, edit the two constants, edit the year filters (filter(year == 2025 ...) for both GDP and population) if the reference year moves, rerun.
Assumptions: sheet Data with three title rows above the header (skip = 3); header columns Country Name, Country Code, Indicator Name, Indicator Code, then one column per year. WLD is excluded. Myanmar is MMR and is recoded to BUR.



Current_GDP_IMF_WEO_2025.csv and population_IMF_WEO_2025.csv

Consumed by: 24_generate_data_exogenous.R (Taiwan only, absent from the World Bank series).
Constants: input_path_GDP_IMF <- file.path(base_dir, "raw", "Current_GDP_IMF_WEO_2025.csv") and input_path_population_IMF <- file.path(base_dir, "raw", "population_IMF_WEO_2025.csv").
To update: export the WEO series NGDPD (GDP, current USD, billions) and LP (population, millions) in the IMF data portal CSV layout, drop them in data/raw/, edit the constants, rerun.
Assumptions: columns DATASET, SERIES_CODE, OBS_MEASURE, COUNTRY, INDICATOR, FREQUENCY, SCALE, then one column per year; the row is selected with COUNTRY == "Taiwan Province of China"; GDP is multiplied by 1e9 and population by 1000, so the SCALE must remain billions and millions.



Global GDP Shares and GDP Growth Assumptions to 2035.xlsx

Consumed by: 20_compute_ag_expenditure_share.R.
Constant: input_path_gdp <- file.path(base_dir, "raw", "Global GDP Shares and GDP Growth Assumptions to 2035.xlsx").
To update: download the macro assumptions table of the new USDA Agricultural Projections, drop it in data/raw/, edit the constant, then review the column positions and the year vector in the script: gdp2025 = g[[2]], growth rates in columns 6 to 10 (g2025 to g2029), the long-run average in column 13, years <- 2025:2034, and the growth vector c(r$g2026, r$g2027, r$g2028, r$g2029, rep(r$gavg, 5)).
Assumptions: the first sheet is read without headers; column 1 holds region labels (footnote markers such as 1/ are stripped) that must match the 40-entry crosswalk xwalk in the script plus the aggregates Asia and Oceania and North Africa used for the OAO and ONA residuals; rows with a non-numeric column 2 are dropped. Everything is by position, so a column inserted by USDA shifts the growth rates silently.



current_GDP_2014_WB.csv and current_GDPpc_2014_WB.csv

Consumed by: 23_compute_NTM_ave.R.
Constants: input_path_GDP <- file.path(base_dir, "raw", "current_GDP_2014_WB.csv") and input_path_GDPpc <- file.path(base_dir, "raw", "current_GDPpc_2014_WB.csv").
To update: only if the NTM reference year (2014, tied to the BACI and WITS 2014 files and the NTM AVE dataset) changes; then all 2014 inputs move together. Export the WDI series for the new year, edit the constants and the column name below.
Assumptions: WDI export layout with columns Series Name, Series Code, Country Name, Country Code, 2014 [YR2014]; the last one is read as X2014..YR2014. after read.csv. Missing values are ... EUU is recoded to EUN, MMR to BUR.



current_GDP_IMF.xls and current_GDPpc_IMF.xls

Consumed by: 23_compute_NTM_ave.R (Taiwan only).
Constants: input_path_GDP_twn <- file.path(base_dir, "raw", "current_GDP_IMF.xls") and input_path_GDPpc_twn <- file.path(base_dir, "raw", "current_GDPpc_IMF.xls").
To update: as above, only with the NTM reference year.
Assumptions: the first sheet’s first column is headed GDP, current prices (Billions of U.S. dollars) and GDP per capita, current prices\n (U.S. dollars per capita) respectively (the header text, including the line break, is used in rename()), followed by one column per year; the column 2014 is read; the row is Taiwan Province of China.

title: Updating raw data
text:
Prices and CPI

2026-06-19 IMF Commodity Prices external-data.xlsx

Consumed by: 20_compute_ag_expenditure_share.R.
Constant: input_path_imf <- file.path(base_dir, "raw", "2026-06-19 IMF Commodity Prices external-data.xlsx").
To update: download the IMF Primary Commodity Prices monthly workbook, drop it in data/raw/, edit the constant, rerun.
Assumptions: sheet External, read without headers. Row 1 holds the commodity codes; the script selects PBARL, PWHEAMT, PCOTTIND, PRICENPQ, PMAIZMT, PSORG, PSOYB, PSMEA, PSOIL (table imf_meta, which also fixes each commodity’s marketing-year start month). Column 1 holds date labels YYYYMm (for example 2025M3); other rows are ignored. Units must stay USD per metric ton, except cotton and sorghum in US cents per pound, because the conversion in 20 and 24 is hard-coded per commodity.



2026-06-19 International Prices FAO Meat.xlsx

Consumed by: 20_compute_ag_expenditure_share.R.
Constant: input_path_fao <- file.path(base_dir, "raw", "2026-06-19 International Prices FAO Meat.xlsx").
To update: export the same ten export-price series from the FAO GIEWS FPMA international prices tool, in the same column order, drop the file in data/raw/, edit the constant, rerun.
Assumptions: sheet data, read without headers; column 2 holds dates MM/DD/YYYY; the meat averages use fixed column positions (columns 3, 4, 5 for beef: United States, Australia, Brazil; 6, 8, 9 for pork: Brazil, EU, United States; 7 and 10 for poultry: Brazil, United States), so adding, removing or reordering a series in the export changes the averages silently. Prices are USD per tonne.



2026-06-24 CPI_US.xlsx

Consumed by: 20_compute_ag_expenditure_share.R.
Constant: input_path_cpi_17 <- file.path(base_dir, "raw", "2026-06-24 CPI_US.xlsx").
To update: extend the annual-average CPI-U series (BLS or FRED CPIAUCNS) in the workbook, recompute CPI_2017 as the annual average divided by the 2017 average, edit the constant, rerun.
Assumptions: sheet Sheet1 with columns year, AVG_CPI, CPI_2017; joined on year, and every year with price data must be present (a missing year yields missing deflated prices). The base year 2017 is fixed by the price units of the model (USD Million (prices of 2017)).

title: Updating raw data
text:
Trade barriers
All files live in data/raw/trade_barriers/. Five of them are not distributed with the repository (two for size, three because of UNCTAD TRAINS and WTO terms): tariff_ave_WITS_2023.csv, tariff_ave_2014_WITS.csv, ag_hs_products.csv, ag_tariff_USA_2014.xls and BACI_HS92_Y2014_V202401b.csv. Their derived products are shipped in data/interim/ and reused by main.R when the raw files are absent. A refresh of any of them requires obtaining the file from its source (query settings in Raw data sources; scripts/fetch_large_raw_data.sh reports which are present and downloads the CEPII file), then rerunning scripts 22 and 23, which rewrite the derived files.

tariff_ave_WITS_2023.csv (not distributed)

Consumed by: 22_compute_tariff_ave.R; its presence is also tested by main.R, which otherwise reuses the shipped data/interim/tariff_ave_region.csv and export_taxes_comm_reg.csv.
Constant: input_path_tariff <- file.path(base_dir, "raw", "trade_barriers/tariff_ave_WITS_2023.csv"), and the file name in main.R (tariff_raw) and in the fetch scripts.
To update: obtain the file from WITS (Advanced Query, TRAINS, all reporters, all partners, all HS6 products, the new year, AVE of applied tariff, CSV export), drop it in the folder, edit the constant, and edit the string year = "2023 (or last observed)" written to the output; rerun. Script 22 then rewrites the two derived files in data/interim/, which are tracked in git.
Assumptions: WITS export columns Reporter (numeric code), Product (HS code, leading zero dropped), DutyType, Simple Average, Tariff Year (read as Simple.Average, Tariff.Year). Only DutyType == "MFN" rows are used. Product codes of 3 or 5 digits get a leading zero; the commodity mapping uses fixed HS4 and HS6 lists, so a nomenclature revision that moves the modeled products to other headings requires editing that mapping. The EU must be reported as one reporter (EUN in country_code_WITS.xlsx).



country_code_WITS.xlsx

Consumed by: 22_compute_tariff_ave.R, 23_compute_NTM_ave.R.
Constant: input_path_code (22) and input_path_WITS_code (23), both file.path(base_dir, "raw", "trade_barriers/country_code_WITS.xlsx").
To update: only if WITS adds reporters; append rows.
Assumptions: first sheet with columns country, ISO3, Reporter (the numeric WITS reporter code). MMR is recoded to BUR.



ave_hs_importer.csv

Consumed by: 23_compute_NTM_ave.R.
Constant: input_path_NTM <- file.path(base_dir, "raw", "trade_barriers/ave_hs_importer.csv").
To update: the World Bank NTM AVE dataset is a one-off release (2014 reference); if a new release appears, all 2014 inputs of the NTM step should move together.
Assumptions: columns importer (ISO3), hs2code (HS6 code despite the name, leading zero dropped), ave1C, ave2C; the AVE is the row sum of the last two.



BACI_HS92_Y2014_V202401b.csv (not distributed)

Consumed by: 23_compute_NTM_ave.R; its presence is also tested by main.R, which otherwise reuses the shipped data/interim/NTM_IMP_ave_region.csv and NTM_EXP_ave_region.csv.
Constant: input_path_trade <- file.path(base_dir, "raw", "trade_barriers/BACI_HS92_Y2014_V202401b.csv"), and the file name in main.R (ntm_raw) and in scripts/fetch_large_raw_data.sh and .bat (BACI_FILE).
To update: scripts/fetch_large_raw_data.sh --download fetches release 202401b and extracts the 2014 file. For a newer BACI release, change the URL and file name in the fetch scripts, in main.R, and in the constant, and update country_codes_V202401b.csv to the matching release. Rerun script 23, which rewrites the NTM derived files in data/interim/.
Assumptions: BACI columns t, i, j, k, v, q (year, exporter code, importer code, HS6 product, value, quantity); HS codes lose their leading zero and get it back in the script. Taiwan is BACI code 490 and Myanmar 104.



country_codes_V202401b.csv

Consumed by: 23_compute_NTM_ave.R.
Constant: input_path_BACI_code <- file.path(base_dir, "raw", "trade_barriers/country_codes_V202401b.csv").
To update: together with the BACI release.
Assumptions: columns country_code, country_name, country_iso2, country_iso3.



ag_hs_products.csv (not distributed)

Consumed by: 23_compute_NTM_ave.R; its presence is also tested by main.R.
Constant: input_path_ag_goods <- file.path(base_dir, "raw", "trade_barriers/ag_hs_products.csv"), plus main.R (ntm_raw) and the fetch scripts.
To update: obtain the WITS product group WTO_HS_Aggri exported as CSV; rarely changes. Rerun script 23, which rewrites the NTM derived files in data/interim/.
Assumptions: WITS layout with a Product column; the row WTO_HS_Aggri is dropped; only the distinct product codes are used.



ag_tariff_USA_2014.xls (not distributed)

Consumed by: 23_compute_NTM_ave.R (source of the HS6 codes that belong to the twelve commodities). When the file is absent the script reads the shipped data/interim/commodity_hs6_mapping.csv (67 HS6 codes) instead; when present it rebuilds and rewrites that mapping.
Constant: input_path_hs6 <- file.path(base_dir, "raw", "trade_barriers/ag_tariff_USA_2014.xls").
To update: rarely; obtain the WTO Tariff and Trade Data export of the United States applied MFN schedule for 2014 (or any HS6 schedule with the modeled products, if the sheet and column below are kept) and rerun script 23.
Assumptions: sheet Applied_MFN, column E from row 6 holds HS codes; 6-digit codes are kept and classified by their HS4 prefix using the same fixed lists as script 22.



tariff_ave_2014_WITS.csv (not distributed)

Consumed by: 23_compute_NTM_ave.R; its presence is also tested by main.R.
Constant: input_path_tariff <- file.path(base_dir, "raw", "trade_barriers/tariff_ave_2014_WITS.csv"), plus main.R (ntm_raw) and the fetch scripts (WITS_FILE).
To update: obtain it manually from WITS (see scripts/fetch_large_raw_data.sh for the query); only with the NTM reference year. Rerun script 23, which rewrites the NTM derived files in data/interim/.
Assumptions: same WITS export layout as tariff_ave_WITS_2023.csv; DutyType == "MFN" rows; Reporter, Product, Simple.Average.



country_region_WB.xlsx

Consumed by: 23_compute_NTM_ave.R (geographic region fixed effects).
Constant: input_path_region <- file.path(base_dir, "raw", "trade_barriers/country_region_WB.xlsx").
To update: download the World Bank country and lending groups workbook, drop it in the folder, edit the constant; check the row range.
Assumptions: sheet List of economies, rows 1 to 219, columns 2 and 3 headed Code and Region. Regions Europe & Central Asia and Middle East & North Africa are merged into Euro-MENA, East Asia & Pacific and South Asia into Asia-Pacific; renamed regions break the merge silently (they become their own fixed-effect group).

title: Updating raw data
text:
Land cost and livestock

AgTFPInternational2023.xlsx

Consumed by: 21_compute_land_cost_share.R.
Constant: input_path_land_share <- file.path(base_dir, "raw", "AgTFPInternational2023.xlsx").
To update: download the new USDA International Agricultural Productivity workbook, drop it in data/raw/, edit the constant, then check the read: sheet = "Cost Shares", rows = 3:182, cols = c(3, 33) and rename(land_share_r =2021-2030).
Assumptions: sheet Cost Shares; column 3 is headed ISO3 on row 3 and column 33 is the land cost share for the latest decade, headed 2021-2030 on row 3 (row 2 carries the block label LAND); rows 4 to 182 are countries. A new vintage will add a decade column and shift the position, and will rename the header, so both the column index and the name must be edited. MMR is recoded to BUR; the EUR share is hard-coded at 0.113 in the script.



variable_costs_2025/ (five workbooks)
U.S. Feed Grains projections to 2035.xlsx, U.S. Rice projections to 2035.xlsx, U.S. Soybeans and products projections to 2035.xlsx, U.S. Upland Cotton projections to 2035.xlsx, U.S. Wheat Projections to 2035.xlsx.

Consumed by: 21_compute_land_cost_share.R.
Constants: input_path_vc_dir <- file.path(base_dir, "raw", "variable_costs_2025") and vc_pattern <- "to 2035" (every file in the folder whose name matches the pattern is read).
To update: create a new folder (for example variable_costs_2026), drop the new USDA Agricultural Projections commodity tables in it, edit input_path_vc_dir and vc_pattern, rerun. Also edit filter(year >= 2024 ...) if the projection start moves.
Assumptions: parsed by labels in column 1 of every sheet: a Table ... U.S. <crop> title (the crop is recognized from the words corn, sorghum, barley, rice, soybean, cotton, wheat; oats are skipped), an Item row whose remaining cells are crop years such as 2025/26, a row starting Variable costs of production, and the next row labeled Per acre holding the values. A retitled table or a renamed row drops the crop silently; check data/interim/variable_costs_us_2025.csv has all seven crops and all years.



FAOSTAT_total_livestock_value_constant_IntlD.csv and FAOSTAT_each_livestock_value_constant_IntlD.csv

Consumed by: 11_compute_feed_use_decomposition.R.
Constants: input_path_total_value, input_path_each_value, each file.path(base_dir, "raw", "<file>").
To update: FAOSTAT QV (Value of Agricultural Production, constant 2014-2016 international dollars). Export the 2015 Livestock aggregate for all countries, and the 2015 values of the five indigenous meat items for all countries; drop the files in data/raw/, edit the constants.
Assumptions: FAOSTAT CSV with columns Area Code (ISO3) (read as Area.Code..ISO3.), Item, Year, Value. Item labels must be exactly Meat of cattle with the bone, fresh or chilled (indigenous), Meat of buffalo, fresh or chilled (indigenous), Meat of pig with the bone, fresh or chilled (indigenous), Meat of chickens, fresh or chilled (indigenous), Meat of turkeys, fresh or chilled (indigenous) and, in the total file, Livestock. FAOSTAT renames items between releases; a renamed item silently drops out of the shares. The total and each-item files must contain a single year.



FAOSTAT_Livestock_Inventory_2024.csv and FAOSTAT_Slaughtered Livestock_2024.csv

Consumed by: 24_generate_data_exogenous.R.
Constants: input_path_liv_inv <- file.path(base_dir, "raw", "FAOSTAT_Livestock_Inventory_2024.csv") and input_path_liv_slg <- file.path(base_dir, "raw", "FAOSTAT_Slaughtered Livestock_2024.csv").
To update: FAOSTAT QCL, elements Stocks and Producing Animals/Slaughtered for the new year, all countries; drop the files in data/raw/, edit the constants, and edit the two occurrences of mutate(Year = 2024) and year = 2024 in the script.
Assumptions: FAOSTAT CSV with columns Area Code (ISO3), Item, Year, Unit, Value. Inventory items Buffalo, Cattle, Chickens, Ducks, Geese, Other birds, Swine / pigs, Turkeys; slaughter items Meat of buffalo, fresh or chilled, Meat of cattle with the bone, fresh or chilled, Meat of chickens, fresh or chilled, Meat of ducks, fresh or chilled, Meat of geese, fresh or chilled, Meat of pigeons and other birds n.e.c., fresh, chilled or frozen, Meat of turkeys, fresh or chilled, Meat of pig with the bone, fresh or chilled. Cattle and pigs are reported in head and poultry in 1,000 head; the script divides the former by 1,000, so the FAOSTAT units must not change.

text:
Moving the analysis period
When the USDA baseline advances a year, the following year constants must move together (all in code/processing/R/):

12_generate_data_targets.R: lst_obsv_yr <- 2025.
30_generate_data_shocks.R: first_yr <- 2025, last_yr <- 2034.
11_compute_feed_use_decomposition.R: filter(year >= 2025).
20_compute_ag_expenditure_share.R: years <- 2025:2034, the GDP level and growth columns (see the GDP shares file above), filter(year == 2025) for the expenditure and the exported share.
21_compute_land_cost_share.R: filter(year >= 2024 ...) and filter(year>=2025).
24_generate_data_exogenous.R: marketing_year == 2025 for prices, year == 2025 for population and GDP, Year = 2024 and year = 2024 for livestock.
The model run: scripts/run_model_unix.sh and .bat default to 2025:2034, and code/model/test/runtests.jl pins the same period for the baseline package.

The package name written by 60_build_input_package.R follows the first year of data_targets.csv automatically.

title: Updating raw data
text:
Checklist for a full refresh

Place the new raw files in data/raw/ and edit the file name constants and year constants listed above. Keep the previous data/processed/ and data/packages/ copies for comparison (they are tracked in git, so git diff and git stash work).
Decide whether scripts 22 and 23 run or are skipped. They run only when their raw inputs that are not distributed are under data/raw/trade_barriers/ (scripts/fetch_large_raw_data.sh reports which of the five are present); otherwise main.R reuses the derived files shipped in data/interim/. A refresh of the trade-barrier sources requires the raw files, and the rerun rewrites the tracked derived files.
Run the pipeline: scripts/run_r_pipeline_unix.sh or scripts\run_r_pipeline_windows.bat (or Rscript main.R from code/processing/). It must end with main.R ... ALL DONE. Read the console for the 50_harmonize_targets: summary line and any warning about unmatched names.
Inspect data/interim/harmonization_log.csv. Expect rows with delta 1 or 2 and status adjusted, on both checks; a status containing outside or a residual larger than 2 points to a broken read in script 10 or a changed baseline layout.
Spot-check the intermediates against the sources: baseline_projections_long.csv for two or three regions, variable_costs_us_2025.csv for all seven crops, international_prices_annual.csv for the last marketing year, and ag_expenditure_shares.csv for plausible shares.
Diff the new data/processed/*.csv against the previous vintage (row counts per attribute, new or missing region-commodity pairs) before accepting them.
Run the model on the new package: scripts/run_model_unix.sh data/packages/baseline_<year>_Input.zip output/baseline_Output.zip <first>:<last> (or the .bat twin). Every year should report a solved status in the solver log.
Check that the neutral run reproduces the new targets: upload the output package to the dashboard (Dashboard). With neutral shocks every ratio of solution to baseline is 1, so “Top # Regional Changes” shows zero percent change for every attribute and year. A nonzero change in yields or extraction rates points at script 50 (derived series); a nonzero change elsewhere points at the harmonization log.
Once validated, refresh the regression reference: code/model/test/expected/baseline_<year>_Input.sha256 and the fixture path in code/model/test/runtests.jl, then julia --project=code/model code/model/test/runtests.jl.
Update Raw data sources (file names and vintage dates), this page, and Processing pipeline if any script header changed.
